thread.label: Genesis 1:25
thread.text: And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

classes.title: My Temple My Choice

precepts.label: Leviticus 11:44
precepts.why:
Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.

thread.label: Genesis 1:26-28
thread.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thin

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” is not talking about all people. The man is Adam, and verse 28 shows it: God blessed them and told them to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” That is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

Genesis 2:7 is read together with it: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Formed from the dust of the ground: we know God is black, Christ is black and the apostles were black. The real Jews are black, and the Caucasian race, Esau as the Bible calls them, is cursed.

Solomon says the same in Wisdom of Solomon 7, that he is “the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, and that God gave him to know “the operation of the elements.” The elements in the soil are the elements in man: oxygen, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, in different percentages. When God made us from the dust, he took from those elements and worked them to form man, the way he formed land and sea. That is what we call the periodic table today, and it is what Esau tries to do with his so-called science: play Frankenstein and try to become God.

But the image goes deeper than the dust and the skin. The breath God breathed in is wisdom, “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” He gave it to us so that we would know better. Being made after his image and likeness is his spirit, the commandments of God.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:24
precepts.why:
After his image and after his likeness means his spirit, the commandments of God. A lot of the time people think the image and likeness only means looking like God. Ephesians 4:24 shows what his image is: “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

That is after the image of God: created in righteousness. The man God made in his image was made to be righteous and holy, not only to share his color.

So being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; you are still the devil. We say the white man is a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black does not make you special unless you are righteous. It is the laws of God that make us special.

precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Genesis says “after our likeness”, and Psalms 17:15 shows what that likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is righteousness. David beholds God's face in righteousness and is satisfied to wake in his likeness. So man made after God's image and likeness was meant to be righteous.

Read with Ephesians 4:24, the new man “created in righteousness and true holiness”, it is plain: black is black, but being made in his image means being black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. We say the white man's a devil, but there's black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous; it is the laws of God that make us special. The dust of the ground made the body; keeping the commandments is what makes us his likeness.

classes.title: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:10
precepts.why:
Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

classes.title: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.label: Job 26:13
precepts.why:
When did the war start? Through the envy of the devil, when he made his move on Adam’s kingdom. And he made that move through Adam’s wife: “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.”

The serpent is Satan, the devil. It says serpent, but it is not talking about a snake; he is called a serpent because he is slick, forked-tongued, tricky. And notice, “which the Lord God had made.” God created him to be exactly who he is. He was subtil because God made him subtil.

Job confirms it: “By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” God formed that crooked serpent, Satan. He is not a rival power that rose up on his own to equal God; he is a creature God made, crooked by design.

So Satan tricked Eve, the weaker vessel, and caused her to sin, and Eve went and convinced her husband to sin. Then the Most High came to deal with Adam, Eve and Satan, and brought judgment on all three. From there God declared the war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”.

That is why we have to know our adversary. The serpent that deceived Eve is the same one we fight today, in his whispers and in his children, and the one who formed him is the one who will judge him.

thread.label: Genesis 3:14-15
thread.text: And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:

classes.title: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.label: Luke 4:5-6
precepts.why:
Satan made his move on Adam through the weaker vessel, and God brought judgment on the serpent, the woman and the man. To the serpent: “Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”. That is not about livestock. This is paradise; he is cursed above every creation God made there. And, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”.

That one line says two things. Man was made from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being, so “all the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: he will be destroyed in the future for what he did. And eating dust means he is on the earth, and the Lord handed him power over it.

Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” When was the power of this earth delivered to Satan? In Genesis 3, what we just read.

And he gave it to whom he would: first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white man in these last days. That is why Esau is able to create all this technology.

Then comes the declaration of war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Back then her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage, and Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants. Today her seed is the twelve tribes of Israel, and his seed is the so-called Caucasians, Edom. And “it shall bruise thy head”, because his seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. Then, “and thou shalt bruise his heel”: the Lord will take down Satan and his children. So when the Bible says to be soldiers of Jesus Christ, we fight Satan, his wicked thoughts and whispers, and we also fight his children, his physical counterpart.

precepts.label: Job 1:6-7
precepts.why:
“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. He goes before the Lord and answers to him.

“And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking up and down in the earth is the dust he eats. In Genesis 3 God said, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Here is that judgment being lived out: his job is to walk the earth to see whom he can tempt and destroy. Satan became the tempter, and that is his judgment; soon he will be destroyed.

It happened after Satan was judged, and it shows the order of things. The power of this world was delivered to him, but he still presents himself before the Lord and reports where he has been.

The word Satan comes from a Hebrew term meaning adversary: accuser, opponent. And the word devil means deceiver. He is the Lord’s adversary and our adversary. And not only the spiritual Satan: his seed, his children, are our adversary too, because God put enmity between his seed and her seed. The so-called white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. That is the war we are in.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:12
precepts.why:
Genesis 4 shows Satan’s children being born in the earth. Eve bare Cain and then Abel; Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth”. The Lord told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” Do good and you will be accepted; do evil and Satan will rule over you. Cain would become the child of Satan and serve him.

Then Cain talked with Abel, “and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him”. That is the fulfillment of Genesis 3:15, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. The enmity started there. Cain, Satan’s seed, killed our forefather: the first murder on the earth and the first blood shed in the war.

John proves Cain was that seed: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” Cain was always evil. His descendants were the children of the devil, and they corrupted everyone on the earth, even the sons of God, until God destroyed the world. All the evil you see Esau doing on the earth today, Cain was doing back then.

Then the sons of God and the sons of the devil came back. Rebekah’s children “struggled together within her”, and the Lord said, “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”. Jacob is the twelve tribes, the so-called Negroes and Hispanics; Esau is the so-called white man. This fight did not start with slavery, Jim Crow or civil rights; it started in the beginning with Cain and Abel, and was reborn as Jacob and Esau: good against evil. Many of our people followed Cain then, and many follow Esau now and have become children of the devil themselves.

Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, born without pigment, as Cain lost his when the earth cursed him. Jacob took hold on his heel, a prophetic sign of Genesis 3:15: our Lord coming to destroy Satan and his children. And when scripture says “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, it was Herod, an Edomite, who “killed James the brother of John with the sword” and took Peter. The devil means the deceiver, and it is interchangeable: the father and his children, who can do nothing without the father that dwells in them.

thread.label: Leviticus 17:11
thread.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.

classes.title: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.label: Romans 5:10-11
precepts.why:
Leviticus says what the blood is for: “it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.” Paul shows whose blood: “For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” When we were breaking God's law, we became his enemies. Being reconciled now, by Christ's life we are going to be saved.

“And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The blood of Christ is what gave us the atonement, so that we can build upon grace. The blood of Christ is more powerful than the animal sacrifice; it is the most powerful thing in this universe.

Read on in the chapter: “For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” By one man's offence death came into the world because of sin, and it reigned from then until today; look at our condition. “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.”

That is the platform we have now. The platform we had under the one man's sin, we got messed up on. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build upon him and do it right because he did it right. It is through mercy we make it to the door, because our righteousness is as filthy rags; so nobody should be boasting of how perfect he is. Christ did not come for the righteous; he came for the sick, so he could heal them. And “in bringing many sons unto glory”, his death brings many sons into glory: a new body and a new mindset. So keep on trying, keep on working, and don't give up.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:2
precepts.why:
“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.” Christ gave himself as a sacrifice for us. His blood on the altar is the atonement Leviticus speaks of: “I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls”.

Likewise, we are going to have to do the same thing for our brothers and our sisters. We have to become their sacrifice. Many don't pay attention to this: when they put you to death out here, the Lord looks at it as a sacrifice. That is why it is said that in Babylon they see your altar. What did they do on the altar? Offer blood sacrifice. They are going to put us to death out here, and that is what the altar represents.

We are unto God “a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish”. The ones who walk the other way are the ones who “in time past” walked “according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. Those children of disobedience are in the churches, in the mosques, in everything, thinking that is the way. Satan works in them because they keep no commandment. The way is through God's law, statutes and commandments, to his son Jesus the Christ.

So walking in love is walking as Christ walked: keeping the commandments, and giving ourselves for our people as he gave himself, an offering the Lord receives as a sweetsmelling savour.

thread.text: And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.

classes.title: The Bold and the Bashful

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:36-37
precepts.why:
This is where the breaking of “the pride of your power” leads. “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies”. Into their minds: mentally and spiritually, you are going to be broken down. Then “the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: no courage. And “they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

“And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.” Think about that spiritually. Take 2026. When black people get mad at other black people, do we show each other mercy, or do we go full-fledged? We even came up with terms for it: turning up, going savage, crashing out. But do we have that same level of aggression toward white police, or the other nations, or the Chinese? Not at all. We will stand and be aggressive with each other all day long, cuss each other out, beat each other up, kill each other. But we will not stand before the other nations. And to be clear, we do not advocate violence on anybody. The point is that the spirit is not the same toward the nations as it is toward each other.

That faintness is on the face of the African brother who said the colonizers left too early, that we are not prepared to rule ourselves. Not only defeated but subdued: low self-esteem, lack of confidence, self-hate, no faith in his own people. It is seen in a whole country left to itself that looks to the white man, to foreign aid and loans, to save it: a mall built under Chinese direction with not a brick out of place, while what our people build for ourselves has uneven steps and lopsided houses. You can’t do nothing right for yourself. That is what comes of low self-esteem.

So this is the fruit of verse 17, “they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you”, and of verse 19, the pride of our power broken. These are the minds the Lord is going to use our brothers to change.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 22:9
thread.text: Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: Sirach 26:19-21
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.” Reading that, we might think only of agriculture or farming, but it is talking about much more than that, and Sirach 26 shows what.

“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” The strangers are the heathen, the other nations. Then it explains how you give your strength to them: “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed.” A fruitful possession means you have a position, you have money, you are rich. Sow it with your own seed means sow it with your own people. You got money? Don't be going and marrying no damn white woman. What a lot of brothers do today, the first thing when they get money, is go marry a heathen. When you marry the heathen when you are rich, you are giving your strength unto strangers.

Instead, deal with your own people: start a family with the woman God created for you, “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Your stock is your nationality, your race, your people. You are a son of God; why would you want to go deal with other nations?

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” When you marry your sisters and bring forth children among your people, your children and your race are magnified. Good descent means your children are not confused about what their nationality is, because you did not sow your seed among all different kinds of heathen women, as our forefathers did in the book of Nehemiah.

That is the law of Deuteronomy 22:9. When we go and deal with other nations, the fruit of the vineyard is defiled: the children brought forth, the descendants, are defiled and confused.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 25:13-15
thread.text: Thou shalt not have in thy bag divers weights, a great and a small.

classes.title: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:11
precepts.why:
“But thou shalt have a perfect and just weight, a perfect and just measure shalt thou have.” The Lord does not like people who are crooked. If you are going to do business, make sure you have a just balance; do not play with the scale and tilt it in your favor.

Solomon shows whose scale it is: “A just weight and balance are the Lord’s: all the weights of the bag are his work.” The just weight belongs to the Lord. So if you are dealing with a just weight and balance, you are in the spirit, and the Most High loves that.

The Most High is not a joke. He gives commandments on what you should do to live, and says keep them so that you may have life. Dealing justly with your brother is love, and “Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” Doing back-dealing with your brother shows no love; that is hatred. By being covetous you break many laws.

That is why the just weight comes with a promise: “that thy days may be lengthened in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.” The scale that is the Lord's is the scale that lengthens your days.

precepts.label: Proverbs 20:10
precepts.why:
“Divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to the Lord.” The great and the small that Deuteronomy forbids in the bag and in the house are both alike. If you are not doing the right dealings in your business, the Lord is looking at you as an abomination.

Eventually he is going to put your lights out, because he already warned you. If you want long life, have a just weight; that is the thing he is pleased in. If you have divers weights and divers measures, the Lord is not pleased, and your days are going to be short.

That is the other side of Deuteronomy 25:15. If a just weight lengthens your days, an unjust balance shortens them. One day somebody is going to realize you have been robbing them, and they are going to kill you. Dudes will kill you for a dollar; you would be surprised what people do. The Bible knows that, and the Lord wrote about it from the very beginning.

Had you been doing your four chapters a day and applying yourself, you would remember scriptures like this, and when the devil tried to tempt you, you would say no: the Bible says the Lord counts it an abomination.

precepts.label: Proverbs 9:17-18
precepts.why:
“Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.” You feel good when you make that extra money from tilting the scale, when you are stealing. It tastes sweet.

“But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.” What he does not know is where it leads: death and condemnation. The one who eats the stolen bread is sitting among the dead.

So do not be a thief. Deal righteously; deal according to the law, statutes and commandments. The divers weights of Deuteronomy 25 are stolen waters, and the days they seem to add are really shortened, just as the law warned: the just weight is “that thy days may be lengthened in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.”

And pride keeps a man from hearing it: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Once people have a little money in their pocket, they feel grown and will not seek counsel, and when everything falls apart, then they want counsel. The scriptures say blessed is he that readeth; if we apply what we read, we will be all right.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:3
precepts.why:
What is going on in 1 Samuel 15? The Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy all the Amalekites and everything they have, every last one of them. The Lord told Saul, wipe these devils out. And he didn’t do it.

The commandment was total: “Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” All that they have. All means everything.

Now hold that against Saul’s answer in verse 20: “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.” Wait a minute: the king is still alive. What do you mean you followed the commandment of the Lord? Saul is playing the defensive, justifying himself, making excuses.

Then verse 21: “But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal.” It wasn’t me, it was the people, it was their fault; I couldn’t do nothing about it. That is bashfulness: you don’t take accountability. The commandment said spare the sheep and oxen not, and Saul brought them back and blamed the people.

So Samuel answered, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” To do what you were told is better than coming back saying, my bad, I thought I understood what you wanted, I decided to do it this way. You fulfill the commandment you were given, and if there is a problem, you say something.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:28
precepts.why:
Saul finally confessed in verse 24: “I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” If you are a leader and you are in fear of your people, or you don’t want them to be mad at you, what can those people do to you? Manipulate you. You are a pushover; they can sway you to the left and to the right. Who is supposed to move you? The Lord, not the people you are supposed to lead. You are not leading the people; you are being led by the people.

Then verse 28: “And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.” Damn.

That is what the bashful spirit costs. Verse 23 already said it: “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.” When you are in that spirit the Lord can’t use you; you are not a good leader. Leadership may see something in you and put you in a position, and then when we question you on certain things you make excuses, or you separate yourself into a bubble with the men under you. You are bashful, you are bringing up a bunch of bashful brothers under you, and you are keeping the brothers under you hostage.

The Lord had made Saul king “When thou wast little in thine own sight”, when he thought he was a nobody. And because he feared the people and would not obey, the kingdom was torn from him and given to his neighbour, David, who was better than he.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:2
precepts.why:
“And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He was scared. This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, what is that going to do to the soldiers under him? It is going to spread.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”: so are they that are under him. “And what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” Whatever man the ruler is, like King Saul, such are all that dwell under him.

Take an example. Some brothers have been here six months, a year maybe, not long, still in regular clothes. Some officers have been here eight, nine, ten years. Those young men in the regular shirts are going to follow the example of the officers in the purple shirts. So if you are bashful, afraid, timid and shy, what does that communicate to them spiritually? That they can be timid, shy, fearful and bashful too. You don’t have to say nothing; your spirit is telling them, it’s okay to be like this, the officer can be fearful and timid, so I’ll follow his example, now I know how to move around in here.

It shall not be so. It shall not be so in here.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 17:12
precepts.why:
Saul saw the host of the Philistines and “was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” What is fear? “For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.”

A soldier broke it down: the succours go into comfort, and fear betrays that comfort. What reason offers is the lies you make up in your head. You trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind which ain’t really there.

And on top of that, fear is a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is basically what you can see with your eyes. Saul looked at the host of the Philistines with his eyes and his heart trembled, instead of trusting the Lord who had made him king.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. But in this aspect we can use it about fear.

We fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother at camp gets unruly with us, he’s got a gun or a knife or whatever, and we fear that. But we don’t fear breaking God’s commandments. That we don’t really fear.

That was Saul. When he “saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” He walked by sight. He feared the Philistines he could see and the people who were scattering from him, but he did not fear transgressing the commandment of the Lord, and it cost him the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 1:7-8
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear.” The Bible says the Lord never gave us that spirit. So the fear Saul had when his heart greatly trembled goes back into a lack of faith.

“But of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” We are supposed to have the spirit of power, love and a sound mind.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” We are not supposed to be ashamed of the testimony of Christ. The bashful brother is ashamed and afraid; the one who has God’s spirit partakes of the afflictions of the gospel by the power of God.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:28
precepts.why:
“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.” This is the level we have to get to: where we are not afraid of those brothers and sisters, and the other nations, that can kill the body and have power over us in this society.

“But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the Lord. We need to fear the Lord, the one who can kill body and soul in hell.

Saul feared the Philistines and feared the people, and not the Lord. So, back to 1 Samuel 28:6: “when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.” The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore. He went to the witch at Endor, the same kind he had put out of the land, and Samuel told him, “the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” Because he was bashful, self-willed, easily manipulated and made excuses, he lost the kingdom. Fear the Most High, not man.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 18:10-11
precepts.why:
This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke: “There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits.” The Lord said none of these would be found among Israel.

Saul had just rid the land of all of them: the soothsayers, the witches, the familiar spirits and the wizards. That is what the woman at En-dor throws back at him: “thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” You trying to get me killed.

Now the Lord has stopped answering him, “neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets”, and the same man who cut them off says, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” Find me a wizard so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place. He is double-minded, breaking the very commandment he had enforced, and he disguises himself and goes by night so no one will see it.

That is where bashfulness leads: self-willed, disobedient, deceitful, making excuses, easily manipulated. Samuel tells him the Lord “is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” The Lord rent the kingdom out of his hand and gave it to David, and Saul and his sons would be with Samuel the next day. “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness.” Saul never believed in himself, so he never believed God; he had Samuel's counsel the whole time and would not listen, and when that guidance was gone he ran to the very thing the law forbade.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:17
precepts.why:
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel”. What happened? Solomon got old. He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he built houses of worship for their individual gods. They did not all serve the same god: Chemosh, Remphan, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of those gods required child sacrifice; some involved sexual orgies. And Israel had to pay taxes for those gods.

Solomon said it himself: “And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.” Madness and folly means all kind of sin. However your mind can go, Solomon went there. When Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee”, but “Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.” That is why Ahijah tore Jeroboam’s new garment into twelve pieces and told him to take ten: the northern kingdom, while one tribe was kept for David’s sake. That is the tabernacle of David that fell.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 30:4-6
precepts.why:
Rehoboam took his father’s throne. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son is supposed to look after his father’s friends.

The old men who stood before Solomon were his father’s friends, and they counselled him: “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.” “But he forsook the counsel of the old men”. And he was like his father in the worst way: Solomon in his old age forced the people to pay tribute to the houses of his wives’ gods, and Rehoboam said, “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” I am going to be worse than my father.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him”. Those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men he asked, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?” To the young men, “What counsel give ye that we may answer this people”? We, all together: y’all are my peers, we are running this thing.

Paul warns about that kind of counsel: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lifted up with pride: I know all the precepts. His head gets big because he thinks he knows it all. That is young men, and that type of spirit will destroy itself.

So that is who Rehoboam looked to, and the young men told him to say, “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.” Some of you in here make that same mistake.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:21
precepts.why:
“And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel”. Sirach tells what that does: “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” You rule people with roughness and pride, you are going to lose your position.

That is what happened to Rehoboam. The ten tribes said “What portion have we in David?” “to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” When he sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, all Israel stoned him to death: you came to collect money? We are not giving you anything. Rehoboam made speed to get up to his chariot and flee to Jerusalem, thinking they would kill him next. “So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.”

We just had a case like that in Cali, and many cases in the states, New York and Texas, where brothers felt that in order to be the leader of the sanctuary they had to rule the people with roughness and pride, and they were taking advantage of the brothers and sisters. No: we had to remove you. Roughness and pride is the losing of authority.

thread.text: And Hezekiah received the letter of the hand of the messengers, and read it: and Hezekiah went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.

classes.title: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:7
precepts.why:
Assyria had already taken the northern kingdom around 722 BC, and around 701 they came for Judah. Their ambassador was talking big: we are going to wipe the floor with you, destroy you and bring you into slavery. Then came a letter of threats. And look at what Hezekiah did with it: he “went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.” He took the letter, spread it out before him, and began to pray: “thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth”.

That is what Peter teaches: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” Sometimes we get in situations and fear comes upon us. Go before the Lord. Whatever the problem is, the Lord knows; go before him and spread it out before him, the way Hezekiah did.

And the Lord answered. Isaiah was not in the room when Hezekiah prayed, but the Lord told him to go to the king and say, “That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.” That is how you know Isaiah was a prophet. Hezekiah cast his care upon the Lord, and that same night one angel smote 185,000 Assyrians.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:36
precepts.why:
The Lord asks Sennacherib, “Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel.” By his messengers he had reproached the Lord with his boasting words, and every one of them came up into the Lord's ears: “thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears”. The same words also remind our people how we have despised the Lord.

Christ said, “every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” We have to be mindful of this. Sometimes we speak frivolous things and don't realize the Most High is recording everything. Idle means idolatrous: every idolatrous word we speak.

Sennacherib's words were recorded and answered: the Lord put his hook in his nose and turned him back the way he came. So be careful what comes out of your mouth; the Most High hears it all and will bring it to account.

precepts.label: Job 11:6
precepts.why:
When you go to the Christian commentaries on Isaiah 33, many of them refer it back to this history: Hezekiah, the king of Assyria, and the angel that wiped them all out. They try to keep every prophecy in the past, as history that already happened. That is why the apologists love to say, that happened already: they read a Christian commentary that said so.

But the scriptures have dual meanings. Job says he “would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” We all want to know the secrets of wisdom, and they are double to that which is written. You read something, but it has a double meaning behind it. That's how the scriptures are written.

So Isaiah 33:1, “Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee!”, was Assyria; but guess who also does that today? The United States of America. To spoil means to rob: the oil of Venezuela, the riches of Libya and of Saddam Hussein, Iran, which did nothing to America. “when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled”. The history of 2 Kings 19 happened, and the same word speaks to our day.

precepts.why:
Who was the Lord talking to in 2 Chronicles 7? Solomon. “if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”, and “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes”, then “will I pluck them up by the roots”. So what was Solomon's problem, outside of the sin itself? Solomon tells it on himself: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.”

That was his problem. He couldn't take correction. He didn't want to hear it; nobody could tell him nothing. That's like some brothers here: they can't be told, they don't want to hear it, they get offended. He was an old, foolish king who could no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all the other problems he had.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that. All wisdom was given to him, and he saw his father's life before his eyes. He was concerned with how the world operated and wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from this world.

So the forsaking that brought the captivity began with a king who could not be admonished. When you keep repeating something to people who can't be told anything, after a while you lose them. That is why we have to be willing to receive correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
The Lord warned Solomon, “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments”; to forsake means to abandon, desert or leave something entirely, a breach of duty, to totally turn your back. Proverbs ties forsaking to hating correction: “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.”

When you have forsaken the way, being corrected is grievous to you. You keep having to be told the same thing over and over, and the one who doesn't want to hear it gets pissed off; he doesn't want to hear it no more. That was Solomon, the old and foolish king who would no more be admonished.

And the end of it is death: “he that hateth reproof shall die.” For Israel it meant being plucked up by the roots out of the land and made a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we are in captivity today. We got jammed up because we would not take correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time the correction comes, he will not accept it. So he gets corrected over and over, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiffnecked. The scriptures don't have that effect on him anymore; there is no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers always getting stood up, and after a while it's, yeah, okay, put me out, I'll be back.

Why does that happen? The word of God is not moving you to change. You can't be the same person you were before; there has to be some type of growth. How do you find yourself doing the same thing you were doing ten years ago? Why, ten years later, does somebody have to motivate you to go do the work? Something is not firing off; something is disconnected.

The word of God is supposed to inspire you to change. The word of God changes you; the word of God can cure you. If you ain't changing, it is one of two things: you are a heathen, or you are a reprobate, and the kingdom ain't for you. So if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

That is the other side of 2 Chronicles 7:14. The Lord will hear and forgive and heal the land when his people humble themselves and turn from their wicked ways. The one who hardens his neck against reproof is suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 8:14
precepts.why:
Manasseh “caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom”. That valley, Gehenna, was where Israel burned its garbage, our refuse; the Muslims call it Gehenna, their hell. Where garbage used to be burned, they burned their children, in honor of Baal.

There was an order to it. In the spring they held orgies in honor of Ashtoreth, the fertility goddess, a black Hamite deity whose star is Venus and whose nose is knocked off the statues. Everyone slept with everyone, and the women got pregnant. Nine months later, in the winter, came the bull god, Baal, the sun god the Egyptians called Apis. The babies were laid on the plates of the brass bull with a fire under it and around it; as they burned they wiggled off into the flame, and drums were beaten to drown out their screams. That is what Manasseh was doing, by the thousands. Carnival babies, Freaknik and the club today are the same worship of that goddess.

Why sacrifice the babies? Ashtoreth gave birth to a baby god, Tammuz, and Tammuz died as an infant. The same way she lost her child, the women had to lose theirs, and the same way she wept for her child, they had to weep for the children they sacrificed on the altar. That is why Jesus is always pictured as a baby with Mary.

Ezekiel saw it: “Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” That is what they had to do once they were in that idolatry: weep for the babies they themselves had sacrificed. And it was worse than what is brought out here.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 12:3-7
precepts.why:
“So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.” Worse than the nations we were killing out of the land for doing the exact same thing. What does that mean? Wisdom of Solomon gives an idea.

“For it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants of thy holy land”. Our fathers were Joshua, Caleb and the elders who succeeded Moses; when we entered the promised land we had to war with the nations already there. The old inhabitants were the Canaanites, the Hamites living in the land before we got there.

“Whom thou hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices”: odious works are filth, evil, vile things, and that is what Manasseh was doing. “And also those merciless murderers of children”: Manasseh did it and had the people do it. “and devourers of man’s flesh, and the feasts of blood”: cannibalism, drinking blood, eating flesh. Who knows what Manasseh was doing, but he was worse than the heathen, so we have to factor this in. “and the parents, that killed with their own hands souls destitute of help”: we were killing our own kids.

“That the land, which thou esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colony of God’s children.” The Lord had us go in and kill those nations out of the land because they were doing these things. Then we got the land, turned around, and did the exact same thing and worse under Manasseh, as Ahab did in his time. Manasseh was one of the worst kings Judah ever had.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:1
precepts.why:
During the Persian captivity we got liberty. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”, and he said that because he knew it was a prophecy. Isaiah had written it: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

Why is that important? Write this down: it was written 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. So when he came of age, he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew that the God of Israel, based on that prophecy, was dealing with him to release his people. It goes into more detail in the writings of Flavius Josephus, how the prophets showed Cyrus what he must do. And he obeyed.

So he made his proclamation to all twelve tribes: “Who is there among you of all his people?” Not just Judah. And whoever chose to stay where they had been living for decades, “let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Some of the northern kingdom went back with Judah; some of the southern kingdom stayed out. Everybody did not go back.

precepts.label: Job 42:5-6
precepts.why:
Job ends where chapter 32 began. There the three men ceased to answer him “because he was righteous in his own eyes”, and Elihu was angry “because he justified himself rather than God.” Here Job says, “I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

Job hated himself and repented. He repented for justifying himself and not God, for being righteous in his own eyes. He had said, I am righteous, this is not supposed to happen to me; I made a covenant with mine eyes, I don't look at other women, I am not weak like Adam, I don't hide sin in my bosom. That was his flaw. He was over-righteous, and the Lord did not like it.

In his own eyes Job did not look at it as though there was a reason God was doing this, that God was trying to make him better. In his mind it was, I am righteous, I am not like this person or that person. So the Bible says, “Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?” That person who tries to act over-righteous just ends up looking fake; nobody knows everything and nobody is perfect.

This is the war within, the war nobody sees. Everything Job suffered before was physical, but Satan was attacking his mind too. The Lord used what Job went through to show him what was inside himself, and that is what Satan's attacks do: they show you things inside yourself. Through all of it Job was made perfect, and he came out of it repenting in dust and ashes, justifying God instead of himself.

Your 9-to-5 is not your purpose; your purpose is to keep his commandments, remember that you are called and requested of God, and magnify his law upon the earth.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:17
precepts.why:
David says it plainly: “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” A sacrifice for the Lord is not so much an animal. What he wants laid on the altar is a broken spirit, a broken and contrite heart, which is a broken mind.

That is the same thing Psalms 34:18 says: “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.” Man by nature is arrogant; we do what we want to do. So the Most High will put you in a position where he has to break you, break you down and shame you, bring you down to the lowest, until you realize: I can't do these things no more, I have to humble myself and do better, for the Lord's sake first and foremost, for my own sake, and for my people's sake as an example.

Isaiah shows where the Lord dwells when he comes near. “the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity” is the Father, and eternity is his domain, the upper room, the top floor. Yet he says, “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.” The Father and his Son deal with and dwell with the humble in spirit.

That broken spirit is the sacrifice worthy of his time. Being haughty and arrogant and offering the best sacrifices is a complete waste of time, because humility comes before honor. That is how Manasseh, a man the law said should die, found mercy: he humbled himself, and God would not despise that broken heart.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 19:13-15
precepts.why:
The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

precepts.label: Proverbs 18:24
precepts.why:
Why is a friend's admonishment the same matter as speaking against your brother? Because friend and brother are synonymous. Proverbs explains it: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

There are some friends that are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50:20 says “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”, the slander lands on the friend who admonished you as much as on your own blood.

A man that has friends must show himself friendly, not turn on the friend who corrects him. And God will not keep silence forever: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” That is Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. “and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God”, and the salvation is only to Israel.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:22
precepts.why:
Psalms 51:16: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” David is saying, you don’t desire sacrifice, otherwise I would give it to you; you don’t care about that either. The Lord revealed to David, I don’t care about sacrifices. And Saul didn’t listen either.

“And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Samuel is asking the question: does the Lord require sacrifices above obeying what he tells you to do?

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” To hearken is to listen and humble yourself. That is better than the fat of rams.

So “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” The sacrifice God accepts is a broken spirit. The animals were just temporary; your mind being broken and humbled is the best sacrifice the Lord desires. You can offer and sacrifice all you want, but make sure you offer with a good heart. “Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.” Once the sacrifices of righteousness are offered, then the bullocks on the altar become acceptable.

precepts.label: Sirach 35:17
precepts.why:
Psalms 51:17 says “a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” Ecclesiasticus 35:17 shows what happens when the humbled one prays.

“The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds.” It pierces the clouds: the Lord hears it. “And till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.”

That is David in Psalms 51. When Nathan confronted him after Bathsheba and Uriah, he did not stay the smartest guy in the room. He said, you are right, I am guilty: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.” He kept the promise he made in Psalms 32:5, “I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid.” He held himself accountable, and you have to hold yourself accountable when it comes to your sins.

The bones that were broken were his humbling: being confronted with his wrong, confessing it and acknowledging it, and the consequences that followed. And out of that broken, humbled place he prayed, “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.” That is the prayer of the humble, the one that pierces the clouds, and it is the same humility that brought mercy to King Manasseh.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:11
precepts.why:
Solomon was knocked down, and David, the man after the Lord's own heart, was knocked down. Did they stay down? No. We are not in the business of staying down; we get knocked down and keep going. Satan tells us to stay down, and some brothers and sisters want you to stay down, but that is not what God said. “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” That is what God is looking for.

So what do we pray when Satan knocks us down? David prayed it: “Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” We pray that the Lord does not remove his Holy Spirit from us, because that is what keeps us standing.

“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.” You have to look at the truth with a joyful and glad heart, because you cannot live without it; it is part of your system, your life. Where else can you go? We do not give up our position; we pray that the Lord keeps strengthening us.

“Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” When we get back up, our job is to teach, because we have been through the trial and tribulation and understand what it takes. We go right back to the business we left off, teaching our people their transgressions so they do not fall into what we fell into. Do we give that up to go sit on the couch, or sit in the back and puff up on evil?

Nobody sees the prayer, the crying at night, the tears when you are home alone thinking, I could have done better. That is the broken and contrite heart God will not despise. Tell Satan to bring it on. With a position or without it, be the same: a trooper. And when a brother is knocked down, do not applaud it; fast and pray for him, because he is still fighting the same battle you are, and your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his.

classes.title: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” God's judgment goes round like a ring, a wheel. It comes around without fail, the last no slower than the first.

The scriptures say God shall be known in his judgments. So when Deuteronomy says that when we sin we will find ourselves back in captivity, in slavery and in prison houses, and we look around and see those conditions, his judgment stands. It is sure, and his prophecies are fulfilled. That is how we show that God is here: so take heed and fear God.

That is the frame for Psalms 94:20: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The 13th Amendment abolished slavery except as punishment for crime. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. Today prison labor makes billions while inmates earn cents an hour. They framed mischief by a law and misled us with democracy and freedom. Slavery did not end; it evolved.

A former warden testified that a young defendant should get life without parole instead of death because the prison could use him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that sweat equity. That is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life but don't kill him, because it is not good for economics.

The throne of iniquity has no fellowship with Christ: not their holidays, not their man-made religions, and no, the president is not God. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal. But the judgment keeps turning like a ring, and what we institute is keeping God's commandments, so that you stay far from all of that.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:48
precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:2
precepts.why:
This is what Christ’s words meant in the Old Testament. The Lord told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.” God is holy, and he says, you shall be holy.

Holiness is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing out of God’s law in Psalms 119:18: the law is given so that his children can become like him.

What makes us perfect? Read on in Psalms 19. “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” The sun, the moon and the stars prove there must be a God; but how much more should you show him in your conversation and your actions, by not sinning? Then: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The law is perfect because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children. It converts us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the redemption of our souls.

Then: “the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were simple, lost through slavery and oppression, calling ourselves anything but who we are. Coming back to understanding that we are the Israelites, and striving for perfection by keeping the law, is our souls being converted. And you cannot come to perfection without trials: gold is tried in the fire.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:12-17
precepts.why:
David says, “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.” Other nations aren't there; they are not mentioned here. Why does it say the city is compact together? Revelation shows the city.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” This is our book. The kingdom is ours. The names on the gates are the tribes that go up.

“And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” So it is 1,500 miles, the length, the breadth and the height all equal, like a square, like a box. That is a city compact together.

“And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” A hundred and forty-four cubits is approximately 216 feet by a man's measure, but it is the measure of the angel, so it is actually larger. That is the Jerusalem the tribes of the Lord go up to.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
David says of Jerusalem, “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” John saw those thrones: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.”

Thrones set, people sitting on them, and judgment given to them. And who are they? The souls “beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

The thrones of judgment in the psalm are real thrones in the kingdom, where the faithful reign with Christ. That is the Jerusalem the tribes go up to, and that is why we pray for its peace: it is a people before it is a place, and those thrones belong to us.

precepts.label: Luke 22:29-30
precepts.why:
The psalm says that in Jerusalem “there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles who sits on them and whom they judge: “And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

Sit on thrones doing what? Judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The thrones of judgment are for Israel, just as the tribes that go up to Jerusalem are “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.”

So don't read all this and try to throw the Chinese and the Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it. The kingdom, the table, the thrones and the judgment all belong to the twelve tribes.

precepts.label: Isaiah 62:7
precepts.why:
David says, “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Some of y'all are busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem.

Isaiah says how to pray for it: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” Give the Lord no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth.

Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place. We are Jerusalem; pray for us. We are not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there. No: they have to be moved out of our land so that we can go back home. That is the peace of Jerusalem, and that is the prayer that gives God no rest until it is done.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 3:15
precepts.why:
“The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge.” Where is that knowledge going to come from? From the leadership. Jeremiah shows it: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

Your pastors could have been the negroes in the world, leaders who just seek after covetousness. But the Lord led you to pastors according to his heart, brothers who are able to help you build and help you see yourself. They feed you with knowledge and understanding, so that is who you seek after.

So why do you keep running away from them? On the quests there are brothers who show up just to have fun. You see them once, turn around, and they are gone for days: they were not on the quest, they were on a cruise. They are not going for any wisdom, knowledge or understanding whatsoever.

That is the fool of Proverbs 15, whose mouth “feedeth on foolishness”: when leadership is in the room, he looks for who he can talk sports or his job with. The man who has understanding seeks the war room and seeks the water from the Bishop, the Deacons, the captains and the officers. That is what leadership is there for, and this whole Bible is about knowledge, wisdom and understanding that we have to seek out.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:16
precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Why? Because of what you were supposed to do first: “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Everything you take on to do, you are supposed to seek counsel. And if you seek counsel and apply it, things are going to go well for you.

But instead of seeking counsel, pride kicks in. I am my own man, I do what I want. A lot of times when brothers have bad dealings with each other, both of them were out of the spirit, because neither one ever asked for counsel: Listen, I want to do this job with so-and-so; what do you think about it?

Once people have a little money in their pocket, they feel grown. I own my own house, I bought it with my own money, I am doing better than you; who are you to counsel me? Then months later, years later, when everything falls apart, now they want counsel. Counsel did not go before that enterprise; pride went before it, and destruction came with it.

You need counsel before, not after. That is why we have to remember the scriptures: blessed is he that readeth, and if we apply what we read, we are going to be all right. Reason and counsel before every action is the cure for the pride that goes before destruction.
