thread.text: For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.

classes.title: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.label: Romans 6:21
precepts.why:
“For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh”. Where your heart is, there will your treasure be: if you are after the flesh, you are going to mind the things of the flesh. “For to be carnally minded is death”. If you stay in that carnal mind, that is death.

Romans 6 goes with it: “What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed?” That is the fruit of the things you now realize were sinful behavior. “for the end of those things is death”. The end of the things you should be ashamed of is death. Paul is dealing with the carnality.

So the death of Romans 8:6 is not a mystery: it is the fruit of minding the flesh. The things we once did in the flesh bore nothing but shame, and their end is death.

Then read Romans 8:5 again with that in mind: “but to be spiritually minded is life and peace”. Notice it is not just life; it is peace. Some of us still have so much drama in our lives because we are not applying this, seeking peace in things that are not God.

precepts.label: Isaiah 26:3
precepts.why:
To be spiritually minded is life and peace, and Isaiah shows where that peace comes from: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.” This is part of the meditation, the daily feeding. If we are not feeding ourselves, we are being pulled away from God.

When we meditate day and night on the Lord, our mind is stayed on him and we build up our trust in him. That is what the second generation had to do in the wilderness that the first generation did not.

It is heavy, because it says to trust in him. People say, it doesn't work for me; that shows they do not trust in God. It is unbelievable how much goes back to your faith. If you are weak in spirit, your faith is weak too. If your faith is only strong when things are going your way, that is not faith at all; if it is only when things benefit you that you feel confident trusting God, then you do not trust in God.

The peace of God overcomes anything you are dealing with or struggling with. If it does not seem to work for you, you are still not applying it: keep your mind stayed on him and trust him, and he keeps you in perfect peace.

thread.text: For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

precepts.label: Amos 3:1-2
precepts.why:
“For whom he did foreknow”. Foreknow means knew from the past. Who did God know from the past? Everybody? The church? No. That has to be stressed, especially on the street, because people are so brainwashed with supersessionism, replacement theology, that they say foreknow means everybody in the church.

Amos settles it: “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. The family God knew is the family he brought up out of Egypt, the children of Israel. So it is no church he is talking about: no Presbyterian, no Catholic, all that garbage.

“therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”. Because he knew us, we were punished.

Paul could have said Judah and Israel plainly, as he does in Hebrews and in Romans 9, but in many of his epistles he uses other words for the 12 tribes. “whom he did foreknow” is one of them: the 12 tribes, the only family on earth he has known.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:25
precepts.why:
“whom he called, them he also justified”. Who is being justified? Isaiah answers: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The only ones being justified are all the seed of Israel. It is not talking about the Catholics, not the Jehovah's Witnesses, not any of those false religions.

That is why there is predestination in the Bible. People love to say there is no such thing, but there is, for the 12 tribes of Israel. We were his people in the past, we are going to be his people today and forevermore; we are predestined to be his chosen forever. Whether we as individuals make it or not is up to each individual.

And “whom he justified, them he also glorified”: the seed of Israel that is justified in the Lord “shall glory.” The whole chain of Romans 8:29-30, foreknown, predestinated, called, justified and glorified, runs through the seed of Israel, whom God will transform into the image of his Son, Christ, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 48:12
precepts.why:
“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. Who did he call? “Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.” Jacob and Israel are his called.

So he is not calling all nations on the planet earth. He is only calling Israel. He is not calling Catholics, Jehovah's Witnesses, Baptists. The teaching that the called are everybody in the church all goes back to replacement theology, which came about through the Catholic church, and then the Protestant church that many of us grew up in, which teaches the same thing.

Put Amos, Isaiah 45 and Isaiah 48 together and Romans 8:29-30 opens up: the ones he foreknew, the ones he called, the ones he justified are the 12 tribes of Israel, predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son.

thread.label: Romans 11:1-6, 26
thread.text: I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
“I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” The answer is no: God has not cast away the 12 tribes of Israel. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” Read that first verse on the street and it tells you what the subject is about.

Paul speaks of “a remnant according to the election of grace.” Who is the elect? Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.” We are the elect. Israel is the elect, not all nations. This is where Paul is getting that from.

Paul even says “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew”: there is that word again, the same as Romans 8:29, so we did not even have to go to Amos 3; Paul deals with it here. Elijah thought he was by himself, but God answered, “I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.” The elect remnant is Israel.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. And so, meaning as a result of all that has been said: all 12 tribes shall be saved. “For this is my covenant unto them”: unto the 12 tribes of Israel, the elect of Isaiah 45.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 10:33
precepts.why:
“And if by grace, then is it no more of works”. A Christian will try to hem you up with that: see, my brother, it's not about works. Christians assume that when Paul used the word works he meant thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. That is not what Paul is talking about at all.

Nehemiah shows what the works are: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Stress that last part: “all the work of the house of our God.” Those are the works Paul is speaking of: the works of the temple, the works of animal sacrifice, the offerings and things of that nature.

So the remnant chosen by grace is not chosen by the temple works of sacrifice and offering; it does not throw away the commandments. The elect of Israel are kept by grace, and all Israel shall be saved.

thread.label: Romans 11:17-21
thread.text: And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree;

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Jeremiah 11:16
precepts.why:
“And if some of the branches be broken off”. The branches broken off are Judah. Jeremiah shows the olive tree and its breaking: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.”

God himself named his people a green olive tree, fair and of goodly fruit. That is the tree Paul speaks of. And the fire kindled on it with a great tumult is how the branches came to be broken.

Why were they broken? Paul answers: “because of unbelief they were broken off”. Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off.

So when the wild olive tree, the northern kingdom, is graffed in among them, it is graffed into God's own green olive tree. “Boast not against the branches”: do not boast against Judah. “thou bearest not the root, but the root thee”. The root is Christ, and Christ is the one that keeps the northern kingdom graffed in with Judah. “Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.”

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:16-17
precepts.why:
“and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them”. That is what Ezekiel 37 shows: “Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”.

“And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.” That is the grafting: the stick of Joseph, Ephraim and the house of Israel, joined to the stick of Judah, and the two become one in God's hand.

So the wild olive tree is not the nations; it is the northern kingdom being joined back with Judah. That is why Paul warns, “Boast not against the branches.” Zechariah 12:7 says the same: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: do not be highminded, do not boast.

“Be not highminded, but fear”. The root that bears the graffed-in branch is Christ, and he is the one that holds the two sticks together as one.

precepts.label: Romans 12:21
precepts.why:
The first step is study, pray and apply: do your research, and then turn from sin. Then we have to learn how to turn all of this evil and mischief into righteousness, from the power of Satan to God, from darkness unto light. Romans 12 lays out the steps: “Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.” Come home, family.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another”: looking out for each other and honoring one another within our marriages, our relationships and our nation. “Not slothful in business”: our business is that we are called by God to magnify the law and increase our faith. “Fervent in spirit; serving the Lord”: doing the work and helping your people. “Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Distributing to the necessity of saints”. What better life to live than to help your people?

And the chapter ends with the sum of it: “Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.” Do not let this world destroy your faith.

How do we overcome? With the good of these commandments and the faith of Christ, and knowing who you are. You overcome that evil with the good of this Bible. Love without dissimulation, brotherly love, fervency, patience and prayer are the good that overcomes the evil around us.

thread.text: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.

classes.title: Prepare Ye War

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 1:7
precepts.why:
“Now it is high time to awake out of sleep”. We see all these things going on and some of y’all still stay asleep, not even paying attention to what is going on in the earth. Y’all crazy as hell. You need to prepare ye war, and the first place to prepare is the mind: guard your mind from fear.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” God gave you power, love and a sound mind. Some of y’all are scared. Christ told them to sell their garment and buy a sword, and some are still scared to buy one. Christ said do it.

There is a time and place for everything under the sun, and that time is going to come. So prepare mentally. We are a nonviolent people; all we want to do is serve the Lord. But we will protect and defend ourselves.

Waking out of sleep means not letting fear keep you from doing what Christ commanded. “Now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”, and a mind given power, love and soundness by God is ready for what is coming.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:8
precepts.why:
Waking out of sleep means staying awake: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

You have to stay sober and vigilant, because the enemy looks for open doors and distracted people. As soon as one of y’all gets distracted from the mission, they are coming. That is why every time somebody leaves, we see who shows up: the damn Christian apologists.

They take you all the way back into the world and have you speaking all manner of evil, but they are not telling you to prepare yourself mentally for what is to come. They are just trying to destroy what we are doing. They are not trying to save your soul. They say they are already saved; they are not saved from the nuclear missiles that are about to drop.

So the one who is asleep is the one the roaring lion devours. It is high time to wake up, stay sober, stay vigilant and stay on the mission, because the adversary is walking about looking for whoever drifts.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:4-5
precepts.why:
“Take heed that no man deceive you.” Prepare ye war: you have to prepare yourself mentally, and part of that is not letting any man deceive you. Do not let deception take you.

“For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” He is telling you that many false prophets and many false Christs are going to rise. And it is happening: there are men online right now literally saying that they are Jesus. Freaking Jesus. Freak ass dude.

Christ said more in the same chapter: “For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets”. That is going to happen, and those who are spiritually asleep will be the ones deceived.

So awaking out of sleep is guarding your mind from deception. The time is late, our salvation is nearer than when we believed, and the deceivers are already here. Take heed.

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20
thread.text: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?

classes.title: Prepare Ye War

precepts.label: Proverbs 24:5
precepts.why:
“What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?” So you have to prepare ye war physically. This is war. Strengthen your body and keep it under control; you are not your own.

“A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.” A wise man is strong, and some of you brothers cannot do ten push-ups. Brothers get upset because the camp sets weight standards, and they can't run worth a damn thing; they cannot run three, four, five miles. Sisters, get in shape too. How the hell are you going to go out and teach when you are unfit?

A pastor once challenged the captain, fat as hell, saying he eats people like him up for dinner. Since he started with dinner, the answer was gluttony: about thirty scriptures of correction on his own church page. Not a debate about the color of Christ first; deal with your health right now.

Diets are not wrong, but you still have to exercise. You can fast seven days and be down ten or fifteen pounds, but the Lord put self-preservation in your DNA: the body goes into saving, starts storing more water and more fat, and it comes back. You have to get out here and work out. You are not getting any younger, and your body is the temple: you must be fit to serve.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 14:33
precepts.why:
“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” Your body is the temple, and you must be fit to serve; you cannot serve the Lord and be unfit.

Paul also says: “For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.” Prepare ye war physically, and keep your house in order, because God is not the author of confusion, and order protects in a crisis.

When this empire collapses and global trade is disrupted, the ones who are ready will be the ones whose bodies are strong and whose houses are in order. A body kept under control and a house kept in order is how we glorify God in the body he bought with a price.

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 10:1-6
thread.text: Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;

classes.title: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 45:5
precepts.why:
“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”. Everybody says the Corinthians were Gentiles. If they were Gentiles, how is it that all their fathers were under the cloud in the wilderness? Reading is fundamental; sometimes it is as simple as that.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. When they try to tell you what baptized means, go to Sirach: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.” That is Moses being given the commandments in the cloud.

The baptism is the receiving of the laws and the doing of the laws, in the faith of Christ; do not leave that part out, because the whole Bible is about Christ. Moses did not dip the six hundred thousand men and all the rest into rivers. Where was the water? The Lord had to provide water from a rock. It all goes back to the commandments, because that represents Christ.

Then “did all eat the same spiritual meat”: the manna, and the law of life and knowledge. “And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Everything in the wilderness was the foreshadowing, the setup, to show the dependency we would need on Christ. Many were overthrown in the wilderness, not by an enemy but by their own lusts, and the way to avoid lusting after those things is to feed yourself on the word of God daily.

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 10:14
thread.text: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.

classes.title: Prepare Ye War

precepts.label: Exodus 20:3-5
precepts.why:
“Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry”. That is in the New Testament, for you black Christians, you black apologists, you black pastors who say the law is done away with. Why would Paul write it if the law was done away? Because it goes right back to Exodus 20: “Thou shalt have no other gods before me”.

“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”. That is where 1 Corinthians 10:14 comes from.

Valentine's Day is idolatry; its origin is Februus and Lupercalia, a fertility rite in which women presented themselves to be struck because it was believed to help with fertility. When you sit up there and celebrate Valentine's Day, you are putting Februus, whoever the hell that is, and Lupercalia before the Lord. What's wrong with Christmas? It's idolatry. Your birthday? Idolatry. Halloween? Idolatry. That's what's wrong with it.

The Lord gave us our own high holy days, in Leviticus 23. The Destruction of Nicanor began last night at sundown, the victory recorded in 1 Maccabees 7 and 2 Maccabees 14 and 15, when Judas Maccabeus defeated and killed Nicanor, the Seleucid Syrian Greek commander who came to crush Israel and threaten the temple. Tonight at sundown begins Purim, when we were saved from being wiped out in the Persian Empire: the enemy was Haman, and the deliverance came through Esther and Mordecai. Our enemies' holidays, the Fourth of July and Christmas, are victories over us. Ours are victories over our enemies. Flee from their idolatry and keep what the Lord gave us.

thread.text: I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

classes.title: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:27
precepts.why:
Christ said, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.” There is that daily again. Paul says it of himself: “I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.” How do you do it? By feeding. You deny the carnal man and feed the spiritual man. Not that you stop eating; you starve the carnal and feed the spiritual.

Paul shows it in chapter 9: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”. That is the dying daily. “lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway”. Paul preached to others, but he knew he would drift if he did not die daily and give life to the spiritual man daily as well.

Romans says the same: “if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.” You cannot do that without constant connection to the scriptures. Many say they are battling depression or sin, but they do not open their Bible every day; they are not battling anything. When somebody with good works and a good reputation moves to the left or the right, it is because they stopped feeding themselves daily. That is scary; we all have to check ourselves.

There is no excuse anymore: you have a Bible with you all the time, on your phone. The pattern runs through the whole book: daily bread, daily mercy, take up your cross daily, daily death, daily renewal. “though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day”. The outward man dies; the inward man must be fed. That is daily bread for a dying man.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 3:18
thread.text: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Daniel 9:2-6
precepts.why:
“But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord”. This book is the glass of the glory of the Lord, and we behold it with an open face. What is the open face? Daniel shows it: “And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes”. He went to God openly by prayer and supplication.

But first, “I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Seeking God openly, he went to the book, the writings of Jeremiah. Then he made his confession: “We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments”.

“Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, which spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.” They would not listen to the servants God sent to show them what they were doing wrong.

So when we really behold his face openly, we “are changed into the same image from glory to glory”. There is supposed to be a change in us when we pray, accept and understand that we have sinned against God. We behold ourselves in these books, and what we see there is there for us to fix. The worst thing to do is deny it, or refuse to hearken to the prophets he sends to show us how to get right.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 4:1-3
precepts.why:
Beholding with open face, we are changed. Then chapter 4: “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not; But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. That is what we are supposed to do when we seek him openly, face to face: renounce the hidden things, the secret sins.

“not walking in craftiness”: not talking too much, trying to find a way to snake around it, “nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.” Blessed is the man whose conscience does not condemn him, because he has examined himself against this book, renounced what he was doing, and no longer does it.

“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. If you do not understand that you have to behold with an open face and renounce sin, you are lost. That is the Christian church: we are no longer under the laws of God, we are under grace, you can't call me a sinner, I've been saved. Bro, what are you talking about? You have not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. You're an undercover homo. You're still fornicating, still smoking weed, effeminate, popping gum with your sister's lip gloss on. You have not renounced it, so you are lost.

If you think you found God while the secret life never changes, your religion is vain. It is a level of insanity to ask God to deal with you and then not do what God says. The change from glory to glory comes only when the hidden things are renounced.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:63
precepts.why:
Paul says we “have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. Why must they be renounced and not hidden? “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.”

God knows your inventions and the thoughts of your heart. He knows them that sin and would hide their sin. You cannot openly seek his face while you are hiding your sins, trying to get around them and not deal with them.

The open face of 2 Corinthians 3:18 is a face with nothing hidden. Beholding the glory of the Lord in his book means seeing what is there about ourselves and bringing it into the light: not walking in craftiness, not snaking around it, not handling the word of God deceitfully.

So the man who hides his sin is not beholding with an open face, and he is not changed into the same image from glory to glory. He only fools himself, because the Lord already knows what he thinks in his heart.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:3-4
precepts.why:
“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. Who are the lost? Ezra shows it: “I brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness have I lost you: for ye have sinned before the Lord your God, and done that thing that is evil before him.”

The gospel is hid to them that are lost: to him that is still in sin and has not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. Those are the ones that are lost, still in sin, refusing to stop being dishonest and living as a sinner. If you think you found God while you live like that, you are lost. Your religion is vain and you do not really believe.

“But what shall I now do unto you? I am a widow and forsaken: go your way, O my children, and ask mercy of the Lord.”

So beholding the glory of the Lord with an open face must bring a change. Christ showed Peter his errors before he was converted, telling him he would deny him thrice, and afterward Peter was the head of the church. God opens his book and shows us, and sends prophets to show us how to get right. It does not feel good, like medicine, but if you are sincere you take it and get better. If you do not, you remain lost, and you become an example of what not to do.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 13:5
thread.text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 6:3
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves”. Every brother and sister must examine themselves, and nobody can prove you but you. Ask yourself what you are doing that keeps you from growing in the spirit of Christ, and what you need help with. Do not wait until you hit rock bottom. The faith is the scriptures, and you must constantly examine yourself to see that you are still in it, because Satan can bind us while we still think we are in the truth, hardly reading, hardly studying, hardly watching class.

Knowing yourself means knowing your triggers and your weak point. If you are covetous, you should not have a job dealing with money. If you are lustful, you should not be watching certain videos or listening to R&B heavy. Music, movies and social media will lead you to porn. My lust and your lust might be different, but if I know myself, I know mine. So when the thought comes you say, self, we ain't going to do that today, turn it off and meditate on the scriptures. If you do not examine yourself, you are reprobate, and you let Satan use your body to do whatever he wants.

Why does it matter so much? “Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed”. Satan wants us to shame the ministry, and he makes us believe it is just a little thing. But people want to prove us wrong. They are ready to pick at any little thing: see what leadership is doing, see what the brothers and sisters are doing. Satan sets people inside the congregations for this, ready to say, I'm offended, I'm leaving.

Yet offences are everywhere. Solomon offended, and the whole of Israel was not destroyed; Israel still went on. One man's sin does not destroy everything, which is why we pray and fast for our leadership to stay on course. So take every little thing as a big thing, keep examining yourself, and do not go back to sin, so that the ministry is not blamed.

thread.label: Galatians 5:16-17
thread.text: This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

classes.title: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.label: Romans 7:14
precepts.why:
“Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” What is the Spirit you have to walk in so that you never do amiss? “For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” The law is spiritual. We are carnal, sold under sin. So if we want to stop being carnal and stop sinning, we have to keep the law.

That is what walking in the Spirit means: walking in the ordinances, the laws, the statutes and the commandments of the Lord God. If you are doing these things, you are never going to do amiss.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”. There is a war within you. The old man always wants to be around, in your business: reading the Bible? You don't need to read the Bible. Let's go rob a house, steal a car, boost cars like you used to, call your man for two birds, go fly some kites. The only way you win this war is by actually reading your Bible and applying what you read.

If you do not read, pray or fast, miss all the new moons and feast days, and show up on the Sabbath just to keep up appearances, you will not be able to fight the lust within your flesh, because you are not walking in the Spirit. The flesh will always be present; it is what you put in you now that fights it. So stay in this book, the spiritual law, and the carnal man is subdued.

precepts.label: John 6:63
precepts.why:
“It is the spirit that quickeneth”: only the spirit can change you as a man. “the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” So when Galatians says walk in the Spirit, it means walk in the words of Christ, the laws, statutes and commandments, and you will not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

Those words have to live in you. The Bible should be like the receptionist at the front desk of an office building: nobody gets in unless she lets them. The door to your soul is your forehead, so the Bible should sit there. When the plan comes up, it says, I hear you, but that's two to five; that's ten to fifteen; that's life. Thou shalt not steal.

When you see a beautiful woman and are tempted to start rubbernecking, you remember Job: I made a covenant with my eyes, why then should I think upon a maid? If you walk in a place and there's a stack of money with nobody around, thou shalt not steal. Without the scriptures readily in your mind, it is impossible not to fall into temptation.

And hidden wickedness does not stay hidden. We are not small any more. A brother making a delivery from another state was recognized by someone not even in the truth. Imagine if he had been doing wickedness. The words of Christ are spirit and life; the flesh profits nothing.

thread.text: For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.

thread.label: Galatians 5:22-23
thread.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:5-9
precepts.why:
“But the fruit of the Spirit is love”: keeping the commandments. Joy: do you have joy in keeping God's commandments, or are you always sad and depressed? Peace with your wife and with the brothers and sisters, not always arguing and fighting. Longsuffering is patience. Gentleness means being right with your brother; it does not mean you have to be soft and act like a sodomite. Faith is believing what the Bible says. Temperance is self-control, not easily provoked. “against such there is no law”, because you are keeping the law. These fruits develop once the word of God dwells in you.

Peter shows the same fruits: “And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge”. Knowledge means learning the scriptures and learning how to break them down, because we are not going to be on social media all the time. Brothers who will not come around the deacons, bishops and officers to learn the knowledge of God are not going to last in this truth. “And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity”: loving God with all your heart and your brother as yourself. All of these are the fruits your tree must bring forth.

“For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Abound means they stay in you. These things can be in you and then leave you. A brother or sister can be among us six or seven years, growing, the leaves green, and then somebody offends them and all of a sudden they stop bearing fruit.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” So examine yourself: am I bearing good fruit? The Lord does not tell you how long he will be patient. A fig tree that bears no fruit is cut down, and a branch that does not abide in Christ withers and is cast into the fire.

thread.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus:

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Psalms 148:14
precepts.why:
Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”. When they try to hem you up with Ephesians 2, before you get to Ephesians 2 you have to deal with Ephesians 1 and 1: who are the saints he is addressing? The Psalms answer it.

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The saints are the children of Israel, a people near unto him. They are the only saints.

There are no saints called Catholics, no saints called Baptists, Methodists or Presbyterians. Taking the name of saints away from Israel and giving it to the churches is supersessionism, replacement theology. So everything that follows in Ephesians 1, the spiritual blessings in heavenly places, the choosing before the foundation of the world, the adoption, the redemption through his blood, is spoken to the saints, and the saints are Israel.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 16:13
precepts.why:
Ephesians 1:4 says “he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”. That is predestination: he chose us before the earth was made. Who is the us that was chosen? David’s psalm says it: “O ye seed of Israel his servant, ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones.”

We are the chosen ones: the seed of Israel, the children of Jacob. There are many precepts on that; Isaiah 44:1 can be used too. With these you could really mess a Christian’s head up, pop his head like a grape. We know the Bible and you don’t. Shut up, listen, and learn.

So when Paul says “Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself”, the ones predestinated and chosen are the same chosen ones of the Old Testament, the children of Jacob.

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
He chose us “that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”. That is difficult for blacks and Latinos: we have hood tendencies. When the videos go up of the fights on the cruise ships, the twerking on cop cars, the twerking in the restaurant a black man opened with his wife, that is not holy.

So how do we become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” In order for us to be the holy people God destines us to be, we must study the law and we must apply the law.

And no, we are not talking about animal sacrifice, because Christians get stupid. We are talking about laws of morality, laws of civility, laws of ceremony, laws of diet. That is what is holy, and that is how the chosen ones become holy and without blame before him.

thread.label: Ephesians 2:2
thread.text: Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:

classes.title: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:1
precepts.why:
“Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world”: we walked according to what everybody else in this world was doing, “according to the prince of the power of the air”, Satan, “the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. The children of disobedience are those in the churches, in the mass, in Islam, in everything, disobeying God's commandments and thinking that is the way. It is not the way. The way is God's law, statutes and commandments, through his Son Jesus the Christ.

Satan is working in our people in the world, because they are not keeping any commandment. So do not listen to your parents talking about how holy they are. Satan is dealing with them, because they are the children of disobedience. How do you disobey God's commandments and call yourself holy?

Isaiah says the same: “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin”. They take counsel, but not of God. They cover with a covering, but not of his spirit.

So if you are not covered with God's spirit, whose spirit are you covered by? Satan's. The rebellious children and the children of disobedience are the same, covered by the prince of the power of the air. The only way out is to come under the covering of God's spirit by keeping his law, statutes and commandments through Christ.

precepts.label: Malachi 4:1
precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom.” Malachi shows how deep that warning really is: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven.” That is why every man and every woman in this truth is warned, and why nobody is played with. Fire is coming for this place. Last time it was water, but the Lord promised that this time it is going to be fire, a fire able to burn the soul, and you feel it while you are in it.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble.” It is their pride and their wickedness that bring the fire on them, so you cannot be prideful. Christ died for your sin; he could have taken you out in that moment, but he gave you grace and mercy. Instead of sitting on your behind, build on the platform of Christ: go out and gather the souls Satan is oppressing, the fatherless and the widow. Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work.

“And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Whatever you are into, it is time to let it go before the fire comes. We fight demons every day, and sometimes it is not that you cannot do a thing; you have to command yourself to do it. Sabbath sickness is a whole slogan for brothers that are lazy bums.

So the life you used to live, the wicked life, died with Christ, giving you a chance before the fire. Now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it. That is the business we are in, in the classroom, on the radio, on TV and in the street: warning people of the destruction to come, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.

thread.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:13
thread.text: But we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: 1 John 2:19
precepts.why:
Paul says, “we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation.” Which of you gives thanks to God every day for the brother or sister sitting next to you? That is the spirit we have to war with from now on: no evil thought of a brother or a sister, but praying and fasting for them, so we may be found faithful in the eyes of God. And it is not a coincidence you are in here. The salvation you are receiving was given to you from the beginning.

How do we know? “They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us.” Some brothers and sisters will come among us who are not of us. If they had been, then no matter what we went through, they would still be with us.

In this body we are going to go through things. This is a hospital; we all need medicine, and the word of God is what heals us. A sister said she left because another sister offended her. How many times have we offended the Lord? We have to build our spirit up so we do not move over every little stupidity.

“But they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They were not the chosen. The same goes for a spouse: if the unbelieving spouse is pleased to dwell with you, they stay because they love you. When a wife or husband gets up and leaves because you came to the truth, that person never really loved you. So you who are still here, it is no coincidence: you were chosen from the beginning.

thread.label: 1 Timothy 4:1
thread.text: Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils;

classes.title: My Temple My Choice

precepts.label: Psalms 119:142
precepts.why:
Christians take this chapter and say every creature is good to eat, so long as you pray over it. But Paul says the meats God created are “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” So what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is the law.

That changes the whole verse. The meat is not received by everybody who bows his head over his plate. It is received by them that know the law. People say, just give thanks, just pray on it, and it's all right. Then can I pray on a human's foot and eat it? Pork carries the worm that lives in the muscle and can go to your brain; the shrimp, the lobster, the catfish and all the shellfish are bottom feeders whose job is to clean the ocean, the roaches of the sea. A prayer does not change what they are.

“For every creature of God is good” means what Genesis means: “God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good to serve its purpose. Worms prepare the land for planting, but we don't eat worms. The pig was the garbage disposal before there were trucks to pick up the garbage. Good for its work, not for your plate.

And Paul finishes: “For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” A Christian never reads up to that verse. The word of God is the law, the truth, and the law is what tells you which creatures are sanctified to eat. Many who have come into the truth, who know Christ is black and that we are Israel, are still struggling with that pork and that shrimp. This is the answer to that struggle: the ones who receive it with thanksgiving are those who know the law.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:24
precepts.why:
Paul says the meats are received “of them which believe and know the truth.” What is it to believe? “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. If you take heed to the commandments, you believe. Does a Christian believe in the commandments? So when he says you can eat anything as long as you receive it with thanksgiving, no: you can pray all you want, but you don't believe and you don't know the truth. Those are the very things that can save your life.

Finish the verse: “and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” If you believe in the commandments and keep the dietary laws, will you be worrying about high blood pressure? Will you be worrying about a foot amputation because of diabetes, about high cholesterol, about gout that takes brothers' fingers and feet? No, because you are not eating in a way where those sicknesses can come your way. The law tells you the food you can eat and the food you cannot eat.

All of that comes because people wanted to eat nasty, dirty food the Lord said don't eat. So take heed to yourself. Believing is not a prayer said over the plate; it is taking heed to the commandment, and the one who does fares never the worse.

precepts.label: Leviticus 11:46
precepts.why:
Paul says the meat “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” So where were the animals sanctified to be eaten or not to be eaten? In the law.

Leviticus 11 closes: “For I am the Lord your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He repeats it: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” How do you become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. To sanctify yourself and be holy you have to apply the law, the statutes and the commandments.

Then: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” This law takes in all the animals, whether they live on the earth or in the waters. That is how the word sanctifies the meat: by making a difference between what can be eaten and what cannot. Some animals are clean, some are unclean. It is basic.

The churches don't want you to learn the Old Testament, because they don't want you to be saved. “Keep my commandments, and live”. If you don't keep the law you are not going to live. John says “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food is sin; eating pork is going to kill you, and overeating is going to kill you.

You are supposed to be the temple of God. If you keep destroying yourself with the way you eat, you are working against what the Lord says, and against the work we are all called here to do. The meat that is received with thanksgiving is the meat the law sanctified.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 6:12
precepts.why:
“Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.” What is our profession? We are prophets, and a prophet’s profession is to teach. All of us are supposed to be teachers. Timothy gives the charge: “Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.”

You cannot get that eternal life if you do not hold on to your profession. How are you going to fight the good fight of faith if you are not holding on to it? Your profession is to go out there and wake up our people. Your profession is to put in work, because faith without works is dead. Your first work is supposed to be in this truth, not your job. The minute we say profession, some think we mean I’m a nurse, I’m a doctor. No.

What good is it for a prophet to do nothing with it? Some of you never travel, never leave the state of Georgia, yet you say I’m a prophet. All Israel is not in Georgia; Israel is scattered to the four corners of the earth. How many of you prophets have a valid passport? Brothers have had passports since they were three. If you don’t have one, you should be ashamed. Get a passport; Donald Trump is going to force you to get one too. We have much work to do.

And “all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” God will bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or evil. So hold fast the profession, fight the fight, and lay hold on eternal life with a high priest who was “in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.”

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 2:6-11
precepts.why:
“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” Why count it joy? Because you are learning about yourself, what you have to fix. Some come to this truth and never knew they deal with a spirit of unforgiveness. They can’t let somebody off the hook for something that happened ten years ago, five years ago; they still harbor it. The word of God reveals it: I struggle with getting past things. Good, because now you can learn how to forgive, and you want forgiveness yourself. That is a trying of your faith, and Paul shows it in Corinthians.

“Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.” He got punished for his action because he was in error. “So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him.” Contrariwise, the opposite side of his punishment: he paid it, now forgive him. Some brothers don’t have the spirit to comfort; they look at the comfort part as weak. Bro, the Bible says forgive and comfort him.

“lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.” If you don’t allow him or her to grow out of the situation, they feel it is hopeless, there is no chance to repent and get right, and you destroy a brother. “Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.” It is not a weak nature to forgive a brother and confirm your love: it’s going to be all right, I see you fighting, you are trying to get right, we are here for you. Not babying him, but not holding him to something he moved on from.

“For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.” He served his punishment; now let’s see the proof of you: can you forgive? “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” One of his devices is unforgiveness. A brother who stole may not be let into your house again; that is not what this is about. But if he hasn’t committed the same infraction again, and you keep saying remember that time you stole, five years later, that is something you are battling within you, and Satan has you. Let patience have her perfect work, “that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

thread.label: James 1:5
thread.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 51:12-21
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.” How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No. You have to study; you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you. As you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, an expert in the law, that you had not known sin but by the law: I didn't know this was covetousness. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

Ecclesiasticus shows the man who asked: “When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.” He seeks wisdom to the end because wisdom will direct your path. “For thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee”: I will thank you because you will deliver me from that evil path.

“I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness.” I redirected what I was doing and directed my soul to wisdom, because wisdom in its pureness will direct my path and save me. You want to be tethered to wisdom because with wisdom you avoid the punishment. That's what we all want: to get ourselves right, to be a better servant, a better husband, a better father. Teach me, God. Well, somebody has to teach you.

“I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.” As you seek her, you start realizing all the issues you have, and the severity of what God is talking about: eternal damnation, some learning it after death by pain. I can't get past this porn, I can't get past lying. At first it sounds good: I put on fringes, we keep the feast days, we turn up. But now I'm learning, damn, I'm a hateful ass brother, I'm a murmurer, I'm a backbiter. My heart is troubled.

Then: “Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.” You come to the house of learning, and somebody is going to teach you how to direct yourself. So now they're teaching you, and now you're mad? Do we understand what we signed up for? You said you wanted wisdom; here it is. No, you don't really want wisdom. You want church.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God: you pray, you ask of God, then you go to a house of learning and you learn. And what are you asking for? “Search me, O God, and know my heart”: know what I think, how I process your information. “try me, and know my thoughts”: I'm asking God to measure me against his word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there's any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That's what we are all asking God to do: show us. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered.

That's why James says, “My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” You count it joy because you asked, show me all my wicked ways so I can fix them. “But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask God to show you, the scripture comes correcting you, and now you're wavering. What are you doing when you waver? Trying to dodge correction.

So when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the sin a person commits so much as what they do afterwards that shows who they are, because none of us is right. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk, and as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses. Blessed is the man that endures it: just listen, learn, and live.

thread.label: James 1:6-8
thread.text: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 4:26
precepts.why:
“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” You ask God in faith to show you about you so you can fix you, knowing he will direct you on the right path. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” Now you have asked God to show you, the scripture comes to you correcting, and you are wavering. What are you trying to do when you waver? You are trying to dodge correction.

Sirach says it: “Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river.” Here is the river, flowing. You are trying to reroute it away from you, trying to make it go another direction. You are dodging correction and making it seem like something it is not.

That is the double minded man, “unstable in all his ways”: always tossed around, forever moving, never straight, never steady, never going head on. With God “is no variableness”; with man there is variableness: jumping all over the place, can’t take it, making excuses, always responding, always having something to say, never listening. Some start answering before you can even finish the sentence; they are not listening to understand, they are listening to respond. A man of wisdom listens from a neutral position, takes in all the information, then discerns whether it fits him.

You said you wanted wisdom. Here it is. So don’t be ashamed to confess your sins, and don’t force the course of the river.

precepts.label: Amos 5:24
precepts.why:
The one who wavers is trying to dodge correction, to force the course of the river. Amos shows the river as it should flow: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”

That is a river. Let judgment run down as waters. Let it run. Don’t waver and try to get around it; don’t try to force the course to divert it. Let judgment come down, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

You asked God to show you your errors, and he is showing you. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” If you keep rerouting the judgment away from yourself, you will not receive the wisdom you asked for. Let it run down on you, accept it, and fix what it shows you.

precepts.label: Micah 7:9
precepts.why:
“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” What is that person saying? He is taking accountability: I will bear the judgment of God, because I have sinned. “until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

Don’t try to get around the cause. Don’t try to deviate from the judgment. Don’t make excuses. Stop wavering. You asked God to show you, he has shown you where you are wrong, and now you are trying to bypass it: maybe I would be better if you brothers called me and checked in on me; it’s your fault. Do you think this is Disney and this is a ride? You can ride that pony by yourself.

Why will he bring me forth to the light? Because I don’t dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults and my errors because I want to get better, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging. We all fall short.

How do you endure in the truth? Listen, learn and live. There is no special recipe: when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. As soon as the medicine comes, people start running. The infraction does not tell who a person is so much as what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? If they can’t, they lose respect. All the big words mean nothing if, as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses because of pride and ego.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:1
precepts.why:
When people come into this faith, the challenge is dealing with the spiritual man as opposed to the carnal man. They pray for wisdom, for discernment, to grow in the truth, and then they will not listen to the men appointed before them, because the carnal man or carnal woman does not see things spiritually. Ezra shows the spirit behind it: “Thus saith the Lord, I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them my commandments by menservants the prophets; whom they would not hear, but despised my counsels.”

God gave his commandments by the prophets to teach the people, and they would not hear the prophets. But whose counsels did they despise? “my counsels”: God’s. The prophets open the scriptures and show you thus saith the Lord to help you overcome what you are dealing with, and when you resist, it is the counsel God truly gave you that you despise. It came through men, but God inspired it.

So whoever brings correction your way, men or women, it is for your benefit, and they are being inspired by the Lord to direct you according to the path you should walk. Be humble, be quiet and listen. They are coming out of the scriptures and showing your error. Learn; this is how we grow. The carnal man will cause you to resist the direction God wants you to grow in, and that is the wavering, double minded man who shall not receive any thing of the Lord.

All scripture is given by inspiration of God for reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness. It is not a book to tote your ego so you feel good. If the Lord showed us who we are, we would be ashamed; it is only the mercy of Christ and his promise that we are here. For us to change, somebody has to tell us what we were doing wrong, and when they do, don’t get mad.

thread.label: James 1:12-15
thread.text: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: James 4:7-8
precepts.why:
“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God.” You want to blame somebody: Lord, it ain’t me, you put that big booty woman in front of me. The Lord says stop, bro. I put the nine millimeter in front of you, but you didn’t shoot yourself; I put the knife in your hand; I put the crack pipe in the room, but you didn’t smoke it. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed is when something appeals to you and you give in; you entertain it. That is on you; that is your choice. God is just showing you what your vice is, and now that is what you are fighting.

When you are tempted, you are supposed to resist. James tells how: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” Submit yourself to God: take the counsel. How do you resist the devil? By first submitting yourself to God.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” How are you going to draw nigh to God? Somebody is going to teach you and you are going to learn; you go to the house of learning. That is what you are doing now. And God will draw nigh to you and give you a way to escape. “Blessed is the man that endureth temptation.” How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You don’t know you can bench 315 until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; you have to lift.

“Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” We just read that in chapter one: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” Now that you hear the correction about how to get right with God, you have excuses. You see the sin in front of you and turn away, like seeing a booger in your nose in the mirror and turning your head; the booger is still there. “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.” The glass is the Bible; you see yourself in it and walk away and forget. You can close the book; you are still a sinner. Submit, resist, draw nigh, and cleanse your hands.

thread.label: James 1:14
thread.text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Mark 7:21
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Lust has nothing to do with love, and love has nothing to do with lust; a lot of us get those two confused. What is a man’s own lust? Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.”

Read on: “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” Adultery and fornication are sins we battle every day. The spirit of murder you see in this world, and our people fight that demon every day. Covetousness we fight every day, because we lust and covet after these things. Deceit is a demon we fight every day.

These come from within. So the battle is not really from the outside; the thing we lust after is within us, and the battlefield is the mind. A brother can be quiet here but fighting major demons; a sister can be quiet but fighting demons. Quiet does not mean humble. Some are bound with their sin.

And this world feeds it. Everything here is a work of sin. They sell sex everywhere; you think you are watching a movie or a karate flick, and they put that nasty thing in there, and down the line you see how people turn to watching porn. The devil is always there, pushing sin. That is why we have to understand this walk and overcome it: every man is drawn away of his own lust, the evil that comes from within his heart.

thread.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:26
precepts.why:
“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous. The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect; an animal could not be spotted. And James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” But we all fall short.

So who is James writing to? “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

thread.label: James 1:25
thread.text: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:8
precepts.why:
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10
precepts.why:
The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

thread.label: James 4:1
thread.text: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: James 3:15-16
precepts.why:
James 4:1 asks, “From whence come wars and fightings among you?” When you are told something you are doing wrong and something in you is adverse to correction, right is coming in and wrong is warring against it. Captains who have sat in counsel know the look: you tell somebody they don't listen, and they squint like they are confused and repeat back what you just said. It ain't their sight that went bad. It is the battle in the mind, manifesting in the face.

James shows where that confusion comes from: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness in it, and there should be no confusion in what is being said. If you were sincere, you would say, show me the lie, help me understand, maybe I am in error. Instead you are confused, because you are warring with what is right and don't want to accept it. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It is deceiving you, the same deceiving we read in chapter one.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you can't move forward. You are a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer, it is being identified to you, and you cannot reason with yourself. You are struggling with yourself, and that is the war in your members.

precepts.label: James 4:10-11
precepts.why:
When a brother starts to correct you and you don't like it, what do brothers start doing? They get mad, they pull away, they hold a grudge, and then they start speaking evil of the ones who corrected them. James says: “Speak not evil one of another, brethren.”

What are you supposed to do instead? “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.” You are supposed to humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, because you know to do good, but you don't want to do it.

That is the war and the fighting of James 4:1, coming out of the lusts that war in your members. The correction comes in, the wrong inside wars against it, and instead of humbling yourself, the war turns outward into speaking evil of your brother. The one who humbles himself stops the war where it starts.

precepts.label: James 4:17
precepts.why:
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” You know that what is being said is right, but you don't want to do it, because you are struggling. What is sin for you? Your sin is what you are struggling with. That is where the war is: you don't want to accept the prophet telling you.

That is all the people in the streets right now. You tell them what they are doing wrong and they are ready to kill you; they want to fight you for teaching the Bible. What's wrong with you? You hate to hear it because it convicts you. It is letting you know your life is in shambles, that you are evil, that you are the devil.

So the wars and fightings of James 4:1 come from knowing to do good and not doing it. The lust you are holding on to wars against the good you already know.

precepts.label: Job 9:20
precepts.why:
Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You are condemning yourself. The word of God, which comes from the teachers, is supposed to cleanse you, and the margin gives justify as cleanse, or clear self. So justifying yourself is deceiving yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear. Whatever the teachers have to say, the reproof and the instruction I'm receiving, I'm already clean.

When that happens, teachers, sometimes you have to let people suffer. Most people don't make the same mistake twice by accident; they choose, ignore the warnings, repeat the patterns, and expect someone else to absorb the consequences. Rescue delays the learning, and growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. David said it was good that he was afflicted. We can't carry everybody.

But teachers and instructors cannot weaponize the scriptures either, using them to correct everybody else and never our own lives. Then you are the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to a higher accountability than you are willing to hold yourself, expecting perfection while you have hidden sins. The justified self is the one the mouth condemns, whether it is the one being corrected or the one correcting.
