thread.label: James 5:12
thread.text: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.

classes.title: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.label: Matthew 5:37
precepts.why:
“let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.” When you say yes, I am going to do it, do it. When you say no, you can’t, then don’t. But never say yes, get paid to do the job, and then not do it. Christ put it this way: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

You are evil when you lie to your brothers. Anything other than yea and nay is evil, and if you are evil you are going to be condemned: not by us, but by the Lord. Condemn means to declare reprehensible, wrong or evil, usually after weighing evidence. The Lord is going to review your case like a court docket: the state versus so-and-so, how do you plead, not guilty, bring the witness. He didn’t know they had the witnesses.

The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good, and he rewards every man according to his deeds. Curse not the king in your chamber, lest a bird carry the news. You do evil in a different state with somebody we never met, and another brother goes to that state for a job and meets the same person. After a joyful Sabbath together, two brothers got in the car, one pocket-dialed the captain, and he heard them talking trash about all the ranking men. When questioned, the first thing was a lie.

When people bring up your evil without anybody asking one question, the Lord is exposing you because he wants you to get right. He could have let you do it to the wrong person, and we find out at your funeral: he stole a hundred grand and a dude put two in his back. You can sit home and hate the messenger, or recognize the mistake, apologize, make amends and walk in the spirit so blessing comes your way. The choice is yours.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:9
precepts.why:
“Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds.” It is forbidden for us to lie one to another. We must be men of character, men of honour, because the world must look at us and say, surely this is a wise and understanding people. If you are lying, how is the world going to say that? They will say this is an evil-ass negro, and the truth gets evil spoken of, because the whole time you were doing it you had fringes on your clothes.

At no time did you look down at your fringes and say, damn, I can’t behave this way, I can’t do this to my brother, not even to people in the world. Why? Because you are not in the Bible. There is no way you are in the Bible and doing evil at the same time; it is an oxymoron. You just finished reading thou shalt not steal, I love that scripture, let me get my gun? It doesn’t go that way. The word has to be nowhere near your head for you to go do evil. That is why you stay in this Bible and give attendance to reading, continuously, so the word is in you.

A bishop “must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.” People in the world will lie on us, but they should never be able to back it up. In business in the world you must be twice as honourable, and you will get more jobs, because nobody likes a thief. Penny wise, pound foolish: make an extra penny now and lose the whole pound. Lie and steal, and you end up ducking people, circling the block, getting beaten over twenty dollars, and still owing the money. The devil convinced you it was okay to lie, then removed himself. Put off the old man and his deeds, and lie not one to another.

classes.title: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.label: Psalms 119:165
precepts.why:
Peter says, “But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye.” We must begin to learn how to suffer for righteousness' sake, for the sake of Christ. And we are happy in it: that happiness is our peace. Happy are they that keep God's laws.

David shows where that peace comes from: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Nothing shall offend them means offenses, and being afraid of tribulation, will not make you turn your back on Christ.

That is why Peter goes on, “and be not afraid of their terror”: the terror of being persecuted. Times are not going to get easy, for husband, wife, brother or sister, so we have to prepare ourselves for hard and trying times and not go railing for railing with one another. Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying and increasing our faith, and following the instructions laid forth.

The man or woman who loves God's law has a peace the world cannot shake. When the tribulation comes, the law they love keeps them from being offended, and they endure it happy, suffering for righteousness' sake.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:1
precepts.why:
Peter laid out the instructions for marriages, because hard times are coming. We see marriage troubles where a sister is upset because her husband's socks are on the floor and she calls him lazy; or a sister gives up the faith and wants to go back to the damn world and be a h-o-e to negro Tyrone instead of a wife to the husband the Lord gave her; or a brother wants to be a whoremonger instead of a man of his nation leading his people. There are more trying times coming, when you will be worried about surviving. How much more in a household where a man and woman are striving and going back and forth with each other?

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives.” Sisters, your tone, how you speak toward your husband, especially in hard times, means a lot. How you respect your lord, your king in your household, and how you carry yourself toward him shows the level of your faith. You sisters have to increase your faith and learn how to be correct with the man God gave you. And not just husband and wife: all you sisters must honor the men of your nation.

In hard times Satan attacks marriage. He did not attack the government Adam set up first; he attacked the foundation, the marriage, which shows how powerful marriage is. And he did it by going through the woman first, which is why you sisters have to build yourselves up.

The Bible says marriage is honorable and the bed undefiled: righteous marriage, husband and wife, as with Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Joseph and Mary, not man and man or woman and woman. Keeping that honorable is part of suffering for righteousness' sake and being happy in it.

Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.label: Sirach 42:24-25
precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another”. God created good, and he created evil also. He “hath made nothing imperfect”: Satan was not created imperfect. He was created to do exactly what he is doing, walking about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

“One thing establisheth the good or another”. What establishes the good of us and makes us perfect? When we go through temptation, when Satan attacks us and we overcome and are not devoured by him. Satan does devour some; some brothers and sisters get devoured. But those that are not devoured become better and become perfect. That is why Peter says “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect”. It is a hard saying, but without Satan, our adversary, we cannot become perfect, because it is his job and his children's job to try us, and as they try us they make us better. Even the real bad things: Job lost all his kids, and that was to make him perfect.

So learn how to fight him and how to see him when he is attacking. See him when he is coming, when he is trying to jump on you and put thoughts in your mind, and say, get out of my mind, Satan. Don't wait until he puts the thought there and you act on it, and afterward you are like Judas, what did I do? That is why the scripture says be vigilant: vigilant means you are watching.

And “who shall be filled with beholding his glory?” Those of us made perfect in trials and tribulation are the ones who will behold the Lord's glory.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:5
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That fire, the furnace of adversity, is temptation. Adversity comes from our adversary, and our adversary is that spiritual demon and his children. So the furnace of adversity in Sirach is the work of the adversary the devil in Peter.

Acceptable men are that gold. When an acceptable man goes through that fire, it doesn't destroy him. It makes him better; it purifies him. When Satan attacks and kills and puts in prison, some men it will destroy, and some men it will make perfect in the sight of God. When the ADL and all these governmental organizations attack us, some of you sisters will be up out of here: I ain't messing with them, the government say they a hate group. Some of you brothers will be gone too. But some of you will be purified and become that pure gold.

You have to go through adversity. Your enemy has to attack you; that is how you become better and how you become a better fighter. Then Peter's words come to pass: “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.” Nobody wants to suffer, but the Lord says if you want the kingdom you have to suffer, and if you are acceptable, after you suffer you will get the kingdom. Suffering makes you perfect, establishes you, strengthens you until you are battle hardened like somebody who has been warring for thirty or forty years, and settles you within your spirit: it is what it is.

precepts.label: Proverbs 30:20
precepts.why:
“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” If you love this place, the love of the Father is not in you. The state of mind of a saint is, I want to be up out of here; I hate this place. All that is in the world is “the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life”, and the lust of the eyes today is TikTok and social media, where the minds of a lot of young brothers and sisters are.

There is a challenge everybody is doing, a dance where they act like they are eating something. The song is called feeling on my body, and it is all about sex. Young brothers and sisters, even among us, watch it and mimic it, and some school sisters were doing that dumb, stupid dance on the new moon. When she says she loves an eater, you think she is talking about eating food? She ain't talking about eating food. She's talking about eating sausage.

The scripture shows what it is: “Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.” She eats and wipes her mouth, and then says she has done no wickedness. That is the characteristic of an adulterous, wicked woman, and that is what the dance is about: sucking rod.

So sisters, you should not be doing those dances. You don't even understand what's behind them. It is the lust of the eyes: you see it on social media and think it's cool. It isn't innocent; you are conjuring demons. We are supposed to be separate, not following the things we see in the world, because the world passeth away, and the lust thereof, “but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.”

precepts.label: Baruch 4:1
precepts.why:
“Blessed is he that readeth”. We all want blessings, and here is the formula. Read four chapters a day and you finish the Bible in a year; if you have more time, read more. Reading is how you hear the word, “and they that hear the words of this prophecy”, and hearing is how you apply it, “and keep those things which are written therein”. You read “thou shalt not steal”, you keep it, and nobody will ever call you a thief. That is how the blessing comes.

But what should you be reading? There are plenty of good books, but this is the book of life. Baruch says: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever”. If you want to know which commandments to follow, you read the whole Bible, and the law endures forever.

So the Christian churches are lost in the sauce. They say you don’t have to keep any laws, yet they keep the one law that actually is done away with, tithing. That proves they are greedy dogs and covetous men, and all their lights are going to be put out. Coming out of that church and seeing that covetousness is a bad thing, why would we come into the truth and still be covetous?

“All they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” If you want life, if you don’t want your light put out, you keep the commandments: read the Bible, learn the laws, statutes and commandments, and apply them. You tell me, do you want life or death? Being here shows you want life; the question is whether you will do what it takes, or revert to the old man and give in to your lust.

thread.text: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a c

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-3
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. Did the literal devil come and cast people into prison? Did a spiritual demon snatch somebody and throw him in a cell? No. When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: it is talking about the father and his children. The same way we can do nothing without our Father and without the Lord in us, these people can do nothing without their father dwelling in them. He uses his children to do what he wants done.

Acts 12 shows who did it: “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.” Herod was a white man, an Edomite. He killed James and put Peter in prison. So at that time the devil casting into prison was Herod, Satan’s children, Rome.

The seed of the devil came back as Esau, and the sons of God came back as Jacob: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Satan means adversary, accuser, opponent: he is the Lord’s adversary and ours, and so is his seed. Devil means deceiver: as he deceived Eve, his children deceive everyone on the earth. That is why we call the so-called white man the devil, because he deceives the whole earth, and Satan, because he is our adversary and God’s.

So know who we are fighting. This is war, and the devil still casts some of us into prison through his children.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
Christ told the apostles, “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”, and he is telling us today these things are going to happen to us. How do we know? “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

You read the scripture say we are going to go to jail. You read that we are going to be afflicted, that tribulation is going to hit us. So wherever you find yourself, when these things happen you remember reading it, and you say, I cannot fight it, this is of the Lord. So you humble yourself to see what he is trying to show you.

That is why you cannot be a snake and think you are going to get away with it, selling your soul for nothing, for a little seventy dollars. The day you are sitting in the furnace of the fire, all of it comes back: the evil thoughts toward your brother, smiling in your brother's face while breaking bread, the things you did in secret against the congregation.

You have your own personal demonic sin you are fighting with. Get rid of that first before you think about lining a brother or a sister up for their failure. What was written aforetime was written so that when the trial comes, you have patience and hope, and you stand.

precepts.label: Psalms 140:4
precepts.why:
Christ said “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, and “be thou faithful unto death”. David shows who is working against us: “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

The purpose of the wicked is to overthrow your goings. You think Satan is sleeping? There is the spiritual Satan and the physical Satan, and every time they are at work, they are working as a team. He will get in your head while you sleep or get in your head while you are awake. At your job, Satan comes jumping into people, and you see people react some type of way.

This is war. That is why you must prepare your soul for the pain that is coming with their children, Esau's children. Whatever state you find yourself in, jail, about to be put to death, afflicted, tortured, losing an eye or an arm, be faithful, because pain is part of the walk. The body is not you; your soul is you.

Mark 9 shows how that spirit works in us: “ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”. That is us destroying ourselves in the club, the partying and religion, because Satan is in us and we thought it was the way. So pray to be kept from the hands of the wicked, and ask the Lord to strengthen your faith, because when your faith is weak, Satan keeps attacking you.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:9
precepts.why:
“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame”. That is the business we are in: we have to overcome. With rank or without rank, a brother has to stay the same trooper. Don’t bail out now; it is time to stand up and face what we have to face.

What we have to overcome, Paul lays out: “Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” Your mother, your father, your aunt, if they are living an unrighteous life, will not inherit the kingdom. “Be not deceived”: not by Christianity, not by religion, not by the white man, not by the uncle or auntie telling you that you are in a cult. Satan can deceive you into leaving this life while you think you are still in the faith.

“Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind”. A lot of us are fighting the fornication spirit, the covetous spirit, the lustful demons. “Nor thieves”: some cannot stop stealing even in this truth, like the brother who borrowed the book and never brought it back. “Nor drunkards”: know your limit, because the drink spirit brings out whatever defilement is in your mind.

“And such were some of you.” That is the life we came from, so don’t think Satan won’t tempt you with these things now. And Galatians 6 warns: “if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work”. It is by the grace of God that you stand. When a brother or sister gets knocked out in this truth, your job is to fast and pray, never to applaud. Be your brother’s keeper; your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his. That is how we overcome.

thread.label: Revelation 7:1-8
thread.text: And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:5
precepts.why:
Four angels hold the four winds of the earth, and another angel cries to them, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The four winds are held back for a reason, and Ezra shows what gathers from those four winds.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” That multitude out of number is their military, gathered from the four winds to fight against Christ, the man that came out of the sea.

So the holding of the winds is this: do not let war pop off to the max until the servants of God are sealed. The armies of the nations are held back until the leaders of Israel, the hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes, are sealed with the law of God in Christ.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
The angel ascending from the east has “the seal of the living God”, and the servants of our God are sealed in their foreheads. What is that seal? Isaiah says it: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is the seal of the living God: the law, sealed among his disciples, in Christ.

And the ones sealed are “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, twelve thousand of every tribe, from Juda to Benjamin. These are the leaders; the 144,000 is just the leading men. In order for them to be sealed, they have to know who they are, at least to some extent.

So how are you going to read that and be confused about the twelve tribes? You just read all of the tribes right there. You can't make this stuff up.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:5
precepts.why:
“I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters”. There is a judgment coming to this place, and nobody wants it judged. Their inward thought is that this kingdom lasts forever. The pride in Esau’s heart says we are in the perfect geographical location, nobody can attack us; meanwhile they go destroy a country and then bring the same people they destroyed over here.

Who sits upon many waters? Put up the map of the US military bases: 845 and more. Who has their navy in everybody’s water, their submarines everywhere? Babylon the great is a world-reaching power over many peoples, nations and tongues, with global influence. The US has launched 469 military interventions since 1798, 251 since 1991. You cannot tell me Babylon is not America.

Habakkuk describes him: “because he transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home, who enlargeth his desire as hell”. He never stays at home. In Vietnam he did the My Lai massacre, murdering hundreds of women, children and old men, raping children as young as twelve, and his Agent Orange still kills people to this day. Look at Iraq; look at Libya, where they are selling Black people for five hundred dollars and no pastor says a word; look at Palestine; look at the proxy war in Ukraine, pumping in billions of weapons. Everywhere he goes he destabilizes the country and it becomes hell.

That is not Saudi Arabia, not the Chinese, not the East Indians. No other nation has that kind of global reach. And he “cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people”. Now the world is shifting to many powers, China and Russia rising, and this place is prophesied to fall. So prepare yourselves, mentally, physically and spiritually: this is war.

precepts.label: Isaiah 5:20
precepts.why:
“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” What are we coming out of? What this society promotes: adultery, the music, murder, sodomy, homosexuality, drunkenness, drug abuse, idolatry, wicked entertainment and corruption. All the things God hates, against his laws, statutes and commandments, and all of it deceives us. We must expose this evil so you can learn how to save your own soul. Look at what they call the YNs: our people smoking, toting guns, women with guns bigger than they are, little kids holding bullets. And then they call us a hate group when we are trying to stop the evil within our own community first.

Sin is deceitful, and America has blurred the line. Your president even asks, what do you have to lose? Choose the worst of both evils. Isaiah 5:20: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Woe is destruction unto them. That is how they blur the line between good and evil.

Who does that? Your pastor. Many a black church on every corner facilitates the continuance of your oppression. So you have to choose a side: righteousness, your heritage, your nation, keeping God’s commandments.

That is the second step: study, pray, apply, see yourself in the scriptures, and then show your faith by separating yourself from evil. Our purpose is Acts 26:18: “To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God”. That is coming out of her.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 1:5
thread.text: Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me; that they may tell their children’s children:

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17-18
precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 1:5 God commands the prophet: “Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds”. Go and show the people. Ezekiel was given the same charge: “get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then God tells him why: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

So as a prophet and teacher, it is required that we tell you what you are doing wrong, because if we don’t, we are liable to have that blood on our hands. It is not that we even have a choice. You call yourself a prophet, a teacher: your job is to go correct the people and help the brother.

That is why showing the people their sinful deeds is not hatred. Sometimes you have to show someone their shame, and that is God loving them too, because he could leave them right there to die and find out after death. It is our job to warn our people, to hopefully bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and they cannot want correction for others while refusing it for themselves.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
If you see a brother that is in error and you don’t correct him, what does the scripture say you are? “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”

If you see a brother in error and do not rebuke him, you hate your brother in your heart. Leaving sin upon him is not love; rebuking him in any wise is. So we have no choice but to tell our people what they are doing wrong, or we hate our brother in our heart.

That is the love behind 2 Esdras 1:5, “shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me”. Showing the people their sins is how you keep from hating them. And it goes both ways: when a brother comes to you and says this is wrong, hear it and learn, because you do not want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

thread.text: For as the husbandman soweth much seed upon the ground, and planteth many trees, and yet the thing that is sown good in his season cometh not up, neither doth all that is planted take root: even so is it of them that are

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
Ezra says the husbandman's seed perishes “if it come not up, and receive not thy rain in due season; or if there come too much rain, and corrupt it”. The husbandman is the Most High, the seed is the word he sows in us, and the rain is wisdom. Anyone who has planted knows that if too much rain falls on a seed, it does not grow. How can too much rain corrupt a man? Paul shows it: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.”

A novice is somebody new in this truth, a beginner. Some brothers come in and catch on real quick. Why would a novice get lifted up with pride? Because he got too much rain, too much wisdom, and he cannot handle it. He starts getting high-minded, and then he falls into the condemnation of the devil: Satan destroys the seed that is in him. That is what it means when the scripture says too much rain can corrupt the seed. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

That is why the heavy teaching is eased off at times. You may love it when the class goes deep, but too much of that wisdom too fast can corrupt you. The deacons have been learning in this truth for over twenty years. When you see them go into certain things, it comes from years of being watered; nobody woke up one day able to break down the scriptures.

So the Most High gives the rain in its season, moderately, as Joel says, “the former rain moderately”, raising the waters little by little, from the ankles to the knees, so that we can handle it. The seed that receives its rain in due season takes root and bears fruit; the novice who is lifted up with pride perishes like the corrupted seed.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.label: Jeremiah 1:5
precepts.why:
Ezra says every one that shall be saved, and shall escape by his works, by keeping the commandments, and by faith in what is written, “Shall be preserved from the said perils, and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.” That is when the kingdom is set up. And why does he say he sanctified them from the beginning? Jeremiah shows it.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Where did he know us? In spirit. This is a physical domain, but he knew us in the spirit world, in another dimension. He did something to our spirit before our parents had relations to bring us forth. You are here because of a conversation God had with you before you even came into this world.

So you people are here because God cares about you. You are not here by accident. There is something in your spirit that God said, I need to fix you, so that when the time comes to destroy the earth, you come back to me and are not in your pride.

The third of Israelites were sanctified from the beginning, from the foundation of the earth. He said, these spirits I am going to love, and these spirits I am going to reject and destroy. God is good all the time to the people that keep his commandments. To you people breaking God’s laws, he is not good. So do not listen to anybody saying God is good all the time; that is not scriptural.

That is why the rest of the chapter is so hard: those who abused his ways, loathed his law while they had liberty and despised the place of repentance “must know it after death by pain.” The sanctified are preserved; the proud are not.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 14:13
thread.text: Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption,

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:9
precepts.why:
“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. Your body is a house; that is the house you live in. Set your life in order, brother, with God's laws, statutes and commandments, and then you can reprove and teach your people. And the Most High has set men over us to do that very work.

“And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.” Our leadership is wise, brothers and sisters; the Lord set them over us for a reason. They teach the people knowledge: how to overcome, how to lead ourselves in the way of righteousness.

Set in order many proverbs: that is what we do when we go over precepts. There are a lot of proverbs we read and don't understand, and leadership puts the puzzle together and sets them in order so you can understand the things of old. “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright”. They search out what the people need and what they are going through. Sometimes they step on toes, just to wake you up or break the chain you have been fighting with.

So God did not leave us without help. When we go off, he set up brothers and sisters to guide us back home. You can never say God did not send help; the one who ignores it is caught up in stupidity.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra to “comfort such of them as be in trouble”, and that comfort comes out of the scriptures: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That which was written was upright, and we have to understand it and follow it. That's the pattern.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. Don't let Satan take it away from you, and don't give it up for Babylon's money; Babylon will destroy your soul. Set your house in order, revive your own soul first, and then revive your people.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:1
precepts.why:
The Lord says to them who keep his commandments and precepts, “let not your sins weigh you down.” Sin feels good. The pleasure comes, and once the pleasure is gone the guilt rolls in, and you feel like crap. After a while it becomes a burden, and it shows on you. Many of us came into the school guilty of things too shameful to confess, and some are still doing them. When you come forward and confess, you feel that weight lifted off: thank God.

Paul uses the same picture: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.” Lay aside every weight. Your sins of character are weights.

If you run a race carrying weights, can you run fast? No. You can still be in the race, but you either keep adding weight until you come in last and never cross the finish line, or you take the weights off. One weight off and you feel lighter; another off and you are faster. You were in third, now second, now first.

Some of y’all say, I’m good back here, I’ll just walk. Meanwhile you are on a timer, and time at the end is running out. A race is won by the time you run. If you are walking in a race, you are not winning at all, by no account.

That is why we lay aside every weight: the sins that so easily beset us are what hold us back. It is what 2 Esdras means: do not let your sins weigh you down.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:76
thread.text: And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Psalms 94:16
precepts.why:
The Lord God says, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” And: “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes.” Brothers give up their position because of the affliction, the little tribulation, or because of their bills, two hundred-some thousand dollars of debt. How could you be that stupid, that ignorant? We all have bills. That is all you have. Their sin is wearing them down so much, and they are so covered with it that they cannot see the brotherhood right in front of them.

David asks the question every one of us has to answer: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” You have to stand up.

The evildoers are where we are today. Taking a man out of his country and bringing him back to America: the same America that pushes democracy, when democracy put him there, kidnaps him and charges him with unjust judgment. Is that just, or wicked? If it is hard for you to see that America is evil, it is because you are evil yourself. Everything here is a work of iniquity; they push sin everywhere, even in a little karate flick.

Christ said, “I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world.” Have the word of God and the world will hate you, and your family will hate you. “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” He left us in the world because we have a path to go through: from Adam until now it has been good against evil, and our job is to stand for what is right. “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The stony ground “immediately receive it with gladness”, but has no root, and when affliction arises “immediately they are offended.” What have you given for this truth? Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are the children of Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you are alive, you still have it. So who will rise up and stand? Do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:11
precepts.why:
“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.” If you are deceitful, that holy spirit of discipline is not going to live with you, and it will not stick around when you are in sin.

Peter names the war: “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”. That includes the lust for food. Overeating and snacking is a fleshly lust warring against your soul, and it drives out the spirit of discipline.

Thoughts “without understanding” are not knowing that we need you to do the work, so we need you healthy; your kids need you and you need yourself. So stop hating yourself and become disciplined. Fix your mind first and don’t say I can’t. Stop overeating, stop snacking, start fasting more, drink water instead of soda and juice, make exercise a lifestyle, eat light, and take care of your body.

Pray and fast that the Lord keeps your discipline. Ask him to change your appetite and strip away the cravings for sugar and processed carbs, and ask the Lord never to remove his holy spirit from you, so you can stay disciplined.

precepts.label: Hebrews 4:12-13
precepts.why:
Wisdom “is the breath of the power of God.” The power of God is the word of God, and the word of God is wisdom. They're all synonymous; they all mean the same thing. The word of God is this book, and the word of God is Christ. It is one pureness, one avenue, with no variableness in what it means. That is why the Christian church has destroyed the minds of a people, making them believe you can separate Christ from the commandments. He is the word. You can't believe on Christ and not keep the commandments, and you can't keep the commandments and not believe on Christ. It's an oxymoron. Yet the witchcraft called Christianity has separated them to the point that it has been said that if you keep the commandments, you're sinning. Your church made you dumb as hell.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Quick means alive. This word is alive; it's not like a textbook. It will affect you to the deepest part of your thought process. It cuts, until you feel sick to your stomach, an emptiness like hunger. If you have never felt that cut in class, examine yourself.

“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” If you are tethered to Christ, you have to be tethered to wisdom, and if you are tethered to Christ and to wisdom, you know BS when you hear it. You know the intention of the heart of a person when they speak. You hear the pity party you've heard a thousand times before. You tell a man, stop talking, and he keeps talking, explaining, digging the ditch deeper, thinking he's making sense and embarrassing himself. A spiritual man discerneth all things. We could be wrong, we're not 100% with everything, we're learning ourselves; but for the most part, tethered to wisdom, you understand false speech.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 36:18-19
precepts.why:
“The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.” Why is one meat better than another? Because you can taste it. You have a palate, and you can say, I like this one better than that one.

“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” The same way your palate can taste which meat is better, a heart of understanding can discern false speech. You listen to somebody and you know: this is BS. It happened recently, around Passover, talking to a brother: listening for a while, it didn't add up, it started to sound like murmuring. You would have been better off keeping quiet, but being that you want to talk, go ahead and embarrass yourself.

That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7 is describing. Wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits.” If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern and understand why people do the things they do: the defense mechanism, the gaslighting, the one in error trying to tug on your heart and make you feel guilty so you will chase him. That's not how this goes. He is supposed to wear down the footsteps.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7-14
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2; it was wisdom, so that we should know better. And what is pure? “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” It will enlighten your spiritual eye to see things clearly, to understand false speech, to know when you're going in the wrong direction. It's supposed to light your path.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.” It is sweet, but then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. That's all right, because the law of God converts the soul. It's only a problem when your soul isn't getting converted.

“Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.” The Lord does not ask us to keep the laws with nothing in return; he is a just and fair God. And converting doesn't just happen; you don't close your eyes and wake up different. It comes through trial, error and correction.

“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults”: things people don't know I'm dealing with. Sometimes a class comes out talking right about you. You said you wanted wisdom. And if it comes in English and you speak Spanish, don't worry: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” We'll translate it, even into sign language. If it's for you, you'll get it. But you need to be cleansed.

“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me.” This is a prayer we ask God for, and then he sends the prophets to tell you. So why are you upset? Don't ask for rain and get mad when it's muddy. You asked God to cleanse you; he has to show you what needs to be cleansed. The first key is listening. The greatest gift a young person can have is to listen: be neutral, hear what's being said, examine yourself whether it's true, and if it is, fix it. Stop lying to yourself.

“then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression. Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.” If you want your words and your thoughts to be acceptable, open this book, learn what the will of God is, and when the word comes to you, accept it for what it says.

precepts.label: Psalms 141:5
precepts.why:
Converting comes through trial, error and correction, and you're supposed to be happy about the correction. “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness”: when that person is telling you what you're doing wrong, it's a kindness that he does it. “and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil”: it's going to be a blessing.

“which shall not break my head.” It isn't going to kill you. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It's supposed to kill the old man in you, not you physically. And people don't want to hear that; they don't want to know the errors of their ways.

When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptations, for trials, for tribulation. People come in with rose-colored glasses, thinking everything's going to be perfect. No: it's going to start unmasking who you are, who I am, and what we have to fix to get right. It's sweet until you start dealing with who you really are. That is the wisdom that leadeth and directeth the wise, as Solomon says: God directs you away from evil and shows you how to avoid it, and his reproof is how he does it.

precepts.label: Psalms 143:5
precepts.why:
Solomon says “the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” To muse, in the Bible, means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, especially God's word or works, often in self communion, prayer and praise: to consider closely, to study in silence.

David uses that very word: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” Listen to the word David used. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer the conditions we suffer. Even Esdras said, Lord, it was not in my mind to know the deep things; I just want to know why Israel is jacked up, why we are going through what we are going through.

All of our minds muse daily upon many things. Why did that person die? Why is my life like this? Where did I go wrong? Should I have married her? Should I have gone to that job interview? Why did I get drunk last night? Most of you can't sleep; you toss and turn every night, especially the man who goes to work every morning carrying the burden of his whole family, or the father up at night thinking about what could happen to his daughters.

This earthy tabernacle, this corruptible body we got from Adam, is what makes us overthink and overanalyze everything. David's musing shows the right place to take it: remember the days of old, and meditate on the works of God's hands, because that is where the answer to why we suffer is found.

precepts.label: Sirach 38:15
precepts.why:
“For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” That belly ache late at night, that belly pain: you are sick. “By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Bible says if you keep overeating, you are going to die. So I guess the Bible is a bully’s book? No. You just hate God and you hate yourself, because loving God is the only way to love yourself. When the white man’s own Department of Health says eight Swedish fish is past a child’s safe arsenic level, you say nothing; when we tell you to stop eating junk, it’s bullying. If you call it bullying, you will not take heed, and you will live a very short life. That is what the Bible says, not what I say.

Then Sirach says: “He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.” What will make you get sick and fall into the hand of the physician? Overeating. The Bible says, if you want to live long, don’t do it. But do we take heed? No, we don’t.

Fat does not stay harmlessly under the skin. Visceral fat wraps around the heart, the lungs, the liver, the stomach and the intestines, and makes your organs work double time, so you always feel weak, tired, low on energy. You don’t feel pain, so you don’t think it’s happening, until one day, bam, stroke; bam, heart attack; high cholesterol, heart bypass surgery. Eating sugar and overeating, you walk around like a ticking time bomb.

That is what we are trying to prevent: you ending up in a hospital bed, in the physician’s hand, because you sinned against your Maker with your mouth. Take heed to what is written, and prolong your life.

classes.title: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “Thou therefore, O Lord, that art the God of the just, hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Obviously: if you are just, you have nothing to repent from. But what makes you just?

Paul answers it: “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The law is holy, and the commandment is holy, just and good. When you are applying it, that is what makes you just. That is what makes you good: the law and the commandment.

So the God of the just is the God of those who keep the commandments, “as to Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, which have not sinned against thee.” They kept God’s laws. Repentance was not appointed for them.

“But thou hast appointed repentance unto me that am a sinner.” Manasseh knew he was not just. He had broken the holy, just and good commandment on every count, and his only hope was the repentance the Lord appoints unto sinners.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:9-11
precepts.why:
Manasseh says the God of the just “hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Paul says the same exact thing: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient.” The law is not made for a righteous man, just as repentance is not appointed for the just.

It is made “for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”, that is homosexuality, “for menstealers”, child traffickers, “for liars, for perjured persons”, liars under oath before the judge, “and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine”, anything not listed.

“According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.” The law is in accordance with the gospel. You cannot have one without the other.

That list is Manasseh. Under the law of Moses he was condemned on all accounts: he killed babies, he was an idolater and a murderer, he shed the blood of children from one end of Jerusalem to the other, and he was steeped in every evil. He was America, but a king; Epstein, but a king; King Diddy Manasseh. There was no animal he could sacrifice. He was a king worthy of death, and his mindset was, I’m the king, I do what I want. The Lord said, you’re the king? Cool, and threw him in prison.

Yet the Lord appointed repentance unto him, and let him live as an example to us in this time. Most kings and celebrities with that status will not repent. When you are rich you become your own god; they literally call them idols. Oprah said on air she does not respect a jealous God. But Manasseh humbled himself, and that is the lesson.

precepts.label: Luke 18:9-14
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “I am not worthy to behold and see the height of heaven for the multitude of mine iniquities.” Many of us think this. Christ gives a parable about that very man, spoken “unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others.” Those who were righteous in their own eyes and despised everybody else were the Pharisees: I'm more righteous than you, you're wicked.

“Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.” The publican was a tax collector, and they were praying in the same place. The Pharisee thanked God he was “not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican”, not like this dude next to him, and bragged, “I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.”

“And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven.” Why? Because he felt unworthy, the same as Manasseh, who could not behold the height of heaven. He “smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner”: the same thing Manasseh said in his prayer, my sins are a multitude.

Christ's judgment: “this man went down to his house justified rather than the other.” The sinner who asked for mercy went home justified; the one who called himself righteous did not. “for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased”: that is what Manasseh did in the beginning, exalting himself, and he was brought down to a low condition, locked up and imprisoned. “and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted”: that is Manasseh later on, after he humbled himself.

So humble yourself and you will be exalted. Exalt yourself and you will be humbled, and you are not going to like that humbling either.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
Manasseh confesses, “I did not thy will, neither kept I thy commandments.” Those two go together, because the Lord's will is his commandments. David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

To do God's will is to have his law in your heart. The laws of God are the will of God; God's will is his laws. So when Manasseh says he did not God's will, he is saying the same thing twice: he did not keep the commandments. Not doing the will of God is not some mystery feeling; it is breaking his law.

That is why Manasseh goes straight on to say, “I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.” He had provoked the Lord's wrath and done evil before him, and he was bowed down with iron bands, locked up with no release. A man who delights to do God's will keeps the law within his heart; Manasseh had to come to that by being humbled, bowing the knee of his heart and acknowledging his iniquity.

classes.title: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:4-17
precepts.why:
Manasseh begs, “forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me not with mine iniquites. Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me.” What does he mean by reserving evil for you? There is evil reserved for you while you keep playing around. Peter shows it.

“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.” These are the angels that fell in Adam’s time, cast down to destruction. Remember David said, take not thy holy spirit from me. If the Lord removes his Holy Spirit from you, you are now in chains of darkness, reserved unto judgment.

“The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.” Manasseh said, don’t reserve evil for me, because the Lord reserves punishment for the unjust. “But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Chiefly means primarily. Despising government is despising leadership. When leadership is trying to help you and you say, nah, I know what I’m doing, you are not humble. Your heart is arrogant.

They follow “the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness”: money. “These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest”, carried about by different doctrines, all over the place, “to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.” The mist of darkness is the reprobate mind; the Holy Spirit is not in them. That is evil reserved for them.

So Manasseh, a king worthy of that very judgment, humbled himself and asked the Lord not to reserve that evil for him. We must do the same while repentance is open.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:7
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me; neither condemn me to the lower parts of the earth.” Peter shows the great evil reserved at the end: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.”

The heavens and the earth are reserved unto fire: nuclear fire, and the hellfire that follows after it. That is what the ungodly are reserved for, and that is what Manasseh was asking not to be reserved for him. The lower parts of the earth he speaks of go into the hellfire again.

Then he says, “For thou art the God, even the God of them that repent.” He is the God of them that repent. Unto them that repent he grants return. So humble yourself before you are sick, examine yourself before judgment, and in the time of sins show repentance, because the fire is already reserved for the ungodly.

thread.label: Prayer of Manasseh 1:13
thread.text: and in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.

classes.title: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.label: Sirach 17:24
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “For thou art the God, even the God of them that repent; and in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.” He is the God of them that repent.

Sirach shows what he does for them: “But unto them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.” Unto them that repent he grants return, return to the land. And he comforts those who failed in patience.

That is the goodness Manasseh expected God to show in him. He was unworthy, a king condemned on every count, but he repented, and the Lord brought him back again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. So it is for Israel as a nation: Manasseh is the living embodiment of the nation, and if we repent, he grants us return.

precepts.label: Sirach 18:20-21
precepts.why:
Manasseh humbled himself in his affliction, and the Lord saved him, unworthy as he was, “according to thy great mercy.” Sirach tells us to do it before the day comes: “Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.”

Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the day of visitation you will find grace and mercy. “Humble thyself before thou be sick, and in the time of sins shew repentance.”

Manasseh waited until he was bound in fetters in Babylon before he humbled himself. Don’t wait until you are sick, locked up, or exposed. In the time of wrong, show repentance, and the same mercy Manasseh found will be there for you.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:2-8
precepts.why:
The Lord is “the God of them that repent”, and repentance is the first thing preached when the kingdom draws near: “Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” It was the first thing Christ said in his preaching, and it goes for all of us.

John the Baptist cried it: “For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.” He wore “raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.” And “Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region round about Jordan” came out and were baptized of him in Jordan, “confessing their sins.”

“But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?” What are you doing here? “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”: fruits suitable for repentance.

That is the fig tree in Luke 13, dunged and dug about so that it may bring forth fruit. That was John’s ministry, paving the way for Christ. Manasseh did not only say sorry; he confessed his sins and his life changed. That is repentance with fruit.

precepts.label: Matthew 9:11-13
precepts.why:
Manasseh says, “thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.” Christ came for exactly such as him. “And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” It is the same spirit as the Pharisee in Luke 18: I’m more righteous than this publican over here.

“But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” That is exactly what Manasseh said: the just need no repentance. The sick are the ones the law is made for, the lawless and the whoremongers.

“But go ye and learn what that meaneth”: go learn what that means, you guys are stupid. “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” He is quoting Hosea. God cares about mercy more than sacrifice. “For I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

God is the God of those that repent. Manasseh had no sacrifice that could cover him under the law, but he found mercy, because Christ came to call sinners like him to repentance.

precepts.label: Hosea 6:6
precepts.why:
When the Pharisees asked why Christ ate with publicans and sinners, he told them, “But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” He was quoting Hosea: “For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.”

God doesn’t care about sacrifice the way the Pharisees did. He cares about mercy. He desires mercy, and the knowledge of God, more than burnt offerings.

That is why Manasseh could be saved. Under the law there was no animal he could sacrifice to cover what he had done; he was finished. But the Lord desired mercy and not sacrifice, and so Manasseh could pray, “in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.”
